Companies like Oracle, Palantir, and Hewlett-Packard Enterprise have moved, while others, including Dropbox, Twitter, and Facebook, have embraced permanent remote work, leading many Bay Area workers to consider leaving the region.

title: Digital ad firm Taboola plans to go public via SPAC
summary: Digital ad company Taboola announced plans to go public through a merger with ION Acquisition Corp., a special acquisition corporation. The transaction, expected to close in Q2, will value Taboola at approximately $2.6 billion and result in the company trading on the NYSE under the symbol TBLA. CEO Adam Singolda emphasized the importance of the open web and Taboola's goal to expand recommendations beyond content to e-commerce, apps, and games across various devices.

title: T. Rowe Price Blue Chip Growth's Manager to Retire
summary: Larry Puglia, the long-standing manager of T. Rowe Price Blue Chip Growth (TRBCX) since its inception in 1993, is set to retire at the end of 2021. Paul Greene, who became associate portfolio manager in January 2020, will officially take over on October 1, 2021, ensuring a smooth transition. The strategy maintains Above Average Process and People ratings and a Silver Morningstar Analyst Rating, reflecting confidence in its continued success despite the managerial change.

title: Google to stop using Apple tool to track iPhone users, avoiding new pop-up warning
summary: Google has announced that its iPhone apps, including Maps and YouTube, will cease using Apple's IDFA tool for personalizing ads. This move comes as Apple prepares to enforce new tracking transparency rules that would require apps to obtain explicit user consent via a pop-up warning, which Google aims to avoid. While Google's core ad business may not be significantly impacted due to its logged-in user base, the company warns that publishers and advertisers relying on its mobile ad software will likely see weaker results without IDFA access.

title: Google & Facebook laws just a back rub for News and Nine
summary: The article argues that proposed Australian laws aimed at making Google and Facebook pay for news content are merely a "back rub" for large media companies like News Corp and Nine, rather than a genuine effort to protect consumers or promote quality journalism. Author Kim Wingerei suggests alternatives to financial penalties, such as licensing search engines and regulating social media platforms as publishers, to address their market power, privacy issues, and the spread of misinformation. He views Google's threat to withdraw services from Australia as a real, albeit last-resort, consequence.

title: Microsoft's Bing ready to step in if Google pulls search from Australia, minister says
summary: Australia's Communications Minister Paul Fletcher stated that Microsoft's Bing is prepared to take over if Google follows through on its threat to withdraw search services from Australia due to the proposed mandatory news code. Fletcher downplayed Google's threat, emphasized that the government would not back down on the code, and highlighted Microsoft's strong interest in expanding Bing's presence in the Australian market. The minister reiterated that companies operating in Australia must comply with its laws.

title: Apple, Its Control Over the iPhone, and The Internet
summary: This article examines Apple's extensive control over the iPhone ecosystem and its implications for the internet, competition, and future digital economies. It argues that Apple's policies, while leading to success, inhibit innovation and create anti-competitive barriers for developers and users through its App Store, payment systems, and technology decisions. The author suggests regulatory intervention to force competition in app distribution and payments, allowing users to download apps from any source and developers to use alternative payment solutions.

title: Here’s how the FAANG companies stack up this earnings season
summary: The article discusses the strong performance of FAANG companies during the earnings season, specifically highlighting their impressive revenue growth and pricing power. This trend continued into the fourth quarter of the previous year and throughout the entire year, even amidst the pandemic. The author notes that these companies consistently deliver significant increases in revenue despite their large size.

title: Waze's ex-CEO says app could have 'grown faster' without Google
summary: Noam Bardin, the former CEO of Waze, stated that the navigation app's growth was stifled under Google's ownership, suggesting it could have grown faster independently. He cited Google's promotion of Google Maps over Waze, Waze's financial losses, and Google imposing constraints while copying Waze's ideas. This sentiment reignites antitrust concerns regarding Google's 2013 acquisition of Waze.

title: Why Are Google and Facebook Now Okay with Australia’s News Media Bargaining Code?
summary: Google and Facebook have come to terms with Australia's News Media Bargaining Code, which mandates payment to news publishers. While initially opposed, their agreements with major news organizations and the inclusion of a compulsory mediation stage have made the legislation more palatable. The Code aims to address the significant bargaining power imbalance between digital platforms and news media, potentially leading to substantial financial contributions for journalism, though concerns remain about media diversity and the focus on larger publishers.

title: You’ve Got a Friend in New Social-Media Apps - WSJ
summary: Dating apps are evolving to focus on platonic friendships, addressing an unmet need for connecting with new people. This shift comes as traditional social media platforms for existing friends are saturated, suggesting a new niche in the social networking market. Bumble BFF, launched in 2016, is an example of this trend.

title: WWE® SuperCard Celebrates 25 Years of “Stone Cold” Steve Austin with New Content Available Now
summary: 2K has announced new content for WWE SuperCard to celebrate the 25th anniversary of "Stone Cold" Steve Austin's WWE debut. Throughout March, players can enjoy new items and events, including a "Stone Cold" Steve Austin cardback, his iconic jean shorts, and a "Stone Cold" Fusion event starting March 9th to create Special Edition cards.

title: Technology and the Free Press: The Need for Healthy Journalism in a Healthy Democracy
summary: This article by Brad Smith, Vice Chair & President of Microsoft, discusses the critical relationship between technology and a healthy free press in a democracy. It highlights how technology, particularly the dominance of companies like Google in digital advertising and content aggregation, has negatively impacted the financial viability of journalism, especially local news. Smith advocates for a multi-faceted solution involving continued evolution within journalism, greater responsibility from tech companies, and government intervention through legislation modeled after Australia's recent law to restore competition and support news organizations.

title: Facebook strikes deal with Murdoch’s News Corp in Australia
summary: News Corp, owned by Rupert Murdoch, has reached a content-supply deal with Facebook in Australia, making it the first major media outlet to do so under Australia's new media laws. The agreement follows a dispute last month where Facebook temporarily blocked all media content in Australia due to the new regulations. While terms were not disclosed, both parties expressed satisfaction with the landmark deal, which aims to transform the economics for journalism.

title: TVA to build state's largest solar site in south central Kentucky
summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) plans to construct Kentucky's largest solar-plus-storage project in Logan County, benefiting Facebook's data centers and General Motors' Corvette Plant. This project, part of TVA's Green Invest program, will provide 145 megawatts of solar power to Facebook and 28 megawatts to GM, along with 120 megawatt-hours of battery storage. It is expected to create over 450 jobs and support the renewable energy goals of both companies.

title: After Spotlight, Snapchat Is Ripping Off Another Core Feature Of TikTok!
summary: Snapchat is reportedly developing a new feature called "Remix," which is similar to TikTok's Duets, allowing users to create new content from friends' snaps by reacting or adding their own video alongside the original. This feature follows Snapchat's earlier launch of Spotlight, a TikTok-like scrollable video feed. The company has confirmed that Remix is currently in external testing, with potential for integration into other parts of the app like Spotlight.

title: U.S. Supreme Court weighs TransUnion bid to nix 'terrorist list' lawsuit
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is considering narrowing a class-action lawsuit against TransUnion, where thousands sought damages after being incorrectly flagged as matching names on a government list of suspected terrorists and drug traffickers. The credit reporting company is appealing a lower court's ruling which upheld a $40 million jury verdict. Justices questioned whether all class members suffered a "concrete injury," a requirement for such lawsuits, particularly for those whose information was not publicly disclosed.

title: As Ad Spending Explodes, Look to These Communications ETFs
summary: The U.S. advertising market is projected to grow significantly in 2021 as businesses increase spending to recover from the pandemic, with an anticipated 15% expansion excluding political advertising. This resurgence is driven by stimulus measures and economic recovery, particularly benefiting digital ad platforms like Facebook and Google. Investors can capitalize on this trend through communication services ETFs such as XLC, FCOM, and VOX, which include major players in the digital advertising space.

title: PT Telkom bangun sistem kabel laut internasional langsung ke Amerika
summary: PT Telkom Indonesia, through its subsidiary Telin, is partnering with Keppel T&T and Facebook to build the Bifrost submarine cable system. This system will directly connect Indonesia, Singapore, and America, spanning over 15,000 km, and is expected to be completed in early 2024. The project aims to strengthen Indonesia's global connectivity with high-speed transmission, advanced technology, and large capacity, supporting the country's digital economy growth and international bandwidth demands.

title: Facebook Built the Perfect Platform for Covid Vaccine Conspiracies
summary: Despite Mark Zuckerberg's stated intention to make Facebook a reliable source for pandemic information, the platform has inadvertently become a major spreader of Covid vaccine misinformation, particularly regarding claims of infertility. The article highlights how individuals like Kaleese Williams, who ventured onto social media for business during lockdown, learned to engage online in ways that could inadvertently amplify such false narratives. This created an environment where vaccine conspiracies could thrive, undermining efforts to disseminate accurate health information.

title: Telkom Gelar Kabel Bawah Laut Langsung ke Amerika Serikat
summary: Telkom Indonesia, in partnership with Keppel Telecommunications & Transportation and Facebook, is building the Bifrost submarine cable communication system. This system will directly connect Indonesia, Singapore, and America, aiming to enhance Indonesia's global connectivity with high speed and large capacity. The project, expected to be completed by early 2024, demonstrates TelkomGroup's commitment to developing digital infrastructure and supporting Indonesia's digital economy.

title: New android malware disguised as Netflix app spreads via WhatsApp message auto-replies
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) has discovered new Android malware, disguised as a Netflix app called FlixOnline, spreading via WhatsApp messages with an auto-reply feature. The malware aims to steal credentials and spread further by offering a fake "free Netflix premium" service. CPR disclosed its findings to Google, which subsequently removed the app, but advises users to be cautious of suspicious links and install security solutions.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | P&G Worked With China Trade Group on Tech to Sidestep Apple Privacy Rules
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) collaborated with a Chinese trade group on a new technology, called CAID, to gather iPhone data for targeted ads. This effort aims to bypass Apple's new iOS 14.5 privacy features, which require user permission for app tracking. The technique, using device fingerprinting, would allow advertisers to continue tracking users despite Apple's policies, which explicitly prohibit such methods.

title: P&G reportedly testing Chinese workaround to Apple’s privacy changes
summary: Procter & Gamble is participating in a test in China of a method to collect iPhone data for ad targeting, as a potential way to circumvent Apple's new privacy features. This initiative, developed with the China Advertising Association, uses "device fingerprinting" technology (CAID) to track online consumers, which violates Apple's app rules. As a major advertiser, P&G is seeking alternative audience tracking methods to maintain ad efficiency given that many consumers are expected to opt out of device tracking.

title: Swvl’s co-founder and former CTO Ahmed Sabbah launches Telda, a Venmo-like app for Gen Z in Egypt
summary: Ahmed Sabbah, co-founder and former CTO of Swvl, has launched Telda, a fintech app aimed at Gen Z in Egypt, similar to Venmo. Telda offers digital accounts with a free Mastercard-powered card for online and in-store payments, cash withdrawals, and facilitates easy money transfers between users. The app has partnered with a local bank to operate in Egypt and plans to expand to Saudi Arabia soon.

title: Reuters introduces online paywall in digital-subscriber push
summary: Reuters is implementing a paywall for its website, Reuters.com, at a cost of US$34.99 per month. This move aligns it with other business news publications like Bloomberg.com and The Wall Street Journal, which already charge for digital access. The initiative aims to attract digital subscribers and was announced shortly after Alessandra Galloni was named Reuters' first female editor-in-chief in its 170-year history.

title: 10 money lessons from some of the world’s most successful people
summary: This article compiles 10 money lessons from highly successful individuals like Oprah Winfrey, Warren Buffett, and Mark Zuckerberg, offering advice on wealth management and financial success. The tips range from practical saving strategies and negotiation techniques to mindset shifts about greed, control, and the importance of investing and valuing small businesses. The overarching theme is that while money is important, understanding its dynamics and having the right perspective are crucial for achieving financial well-being and making a broader impact.

title: Marvell closes on $10 billion Inphi deal, expanding data center and 5G business
summary: Marvell Technology has completed its $10 billion acquisition of Inphi after receiving approval from Chinese regulators, expanding its reach into data centers and 5G network infrastructure. CEO Matt Murphy noted the deal's overwhelmingly positive global customer support. The acquisition will enhance Marvell's growth in key markets such as 5G, cloud, and automotive, and Inphi's former CEO, Dr. Ford Tamer, has joined Marvell's board.

title: The ARKW ETF: Leading the Future of Advertising
summary: The ARK Web x.0 ETF (ARKW) is an actively managed ETF focused on disruptive growth and internet-driven themes, including internet advertising. The article highlights ARKW's leverage to the increasing shift towards digital advertising, particularly as retail footprints decline. It projects significant growth in US digital ad spending, suggesting its critical role in the future economy.

title: Apple and Google Are Killing the (Ad) Cookie. Here’s Why
summary: Apple and Google are implementing separate changes that will effectively end the use of third-party advertising cookies, significantly altering how marketers track online activity and target ads. Apple is requiring app developers to gain user permission for tracking across apps and websites, while Google is developing a cookie alternative that allows for targeted advertising without relying on individual web history. Both tech giants cite privacy as the driving force behind these changes, though Google also emphasizes balancing privacy with the financial viability of web publishing.

title: What do Apple’s new privacy settings mean for you?
summary: Apple is rolling out new privacy settings requiring app developers to explicitly ask users for permission to track their browsing habits across other apps and websites. This change is expected to significantly impact the mobile advertising market as many users are anticipated to decline tracking, potentially reducing ad effectiveness and revenue for businesses and publishers. The move has created a rift with companies like Facebook, which argues it will harm small businesses.

title: Goodwill® Partners With Facebook Elevate And Coursera For Social Media Marketing Training
summary: Goodwill, Facebook Elevate, and Coursera have partnered to offer a social media marketing training program to 6,000 job seekers, particularly focusing on Black learners. This initiative aims to equip participants with digital skills for entry-level social media marketing roles through a 20-week online course, addressing the increasing demand for digital skills in the workforce. The program includes scholarships to cover costs and career support, aiming to increase diversity and break down barriers in the rapidly growing field.

title: Google (GOOGL) stock hits all-time high on Q1 2021 earnings, announces $50 billion buyback
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) reported record Q1 2021 earnings, with revenues of $55.31 billion and EPS of $26.29, significantly beating analyst estimates. Google's stock hit an all-time high of over $2400/share in after-hours trading following the announcement. The company also announced a new $50 billion share repurchase program for its Class C capital stock.

title: Looking for an ETF to Hold for the Long-Term?
summary: The article suggests the Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth ETF (SCHG) as a long-term investment option, highlighting its strong performance and holdings in major growth companies. It emphasizes the potential for significant long-term returns through consistent investing in such ETFs, despite the allure of instant gratification.

title: I'm Not Turning Off App Tracking On My iPhone, Because I’m A Total Cuck
summary: The author humorously explains her decision to not disable app tracking on her iPhone, despite Apple's new privacy feature allowing users to opt out. She describes herself as a "datacuck" who enjoys personalized ads and wants to see "how far this goes" when it comes to data collection, contrasting her personal choice with the recommended smart privacy practices. The article satirically delves into the perceived benefits of targeted advertising while acknowledging the serious implications of data privacy and Facebook's track record.

title: Manhattan Office Struggles May Have Already Bottomed Out: Vornado CEO
summary: Vornado Realty Trust is observing increased demand for its New York City office portfolio, suggesting that the negative impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on the leasing market may be receding. The company's CEO, Steven Roth, and President/CFO Michael Franco, noted an acceleration in leasing activity, particularly in Midtown Manhattan, and a reduction in sublease space. Major technology companies like Facebook are looking to expand their New York footprints, indicating a potential shift from a tenant market to a landlord market in the near future.

title: Apple's conflict with Facebook goes back to the days of Steve Jobs, emails show
summary: Internal Apple emails from 2011 involving Steve Jobs, Scott Forstall, and Phil Schiller reveal that the conflict between Apple and Facebook over App Store rules dates back a decade. Jobs referred to Facebook as "Fecebooks" and believed it shouldn't host its own apps, contributing to the delayed release of Facebook's iPad app. This historical tension sheds light on the ongoing disputes between the two tech giants regarding App Store policies and user privacy.

title: Walmart, Tesla Added to S&P ESG Index, While Victoria's Secret-Owner and Facebook Get the Boot
summary: The S&P 500's ESG Index underwent its annual adjustments, adding 45 stocks including Tesla, Disney, Walmart, and Etsy, while dropping 21 companies such as Facebook, Victoria's Secret-owner L Brands, and Costco. Tesla was included due to its clean energy efforts, and Walmart for improvements in human rights. Facebook was removed for deteriorating environmental reporting, and L Brands for poor ESG performance compared to peers.

title: Lo que necesitas saber para empezar a vender por redes sociales
summary: This article from Bancolombia provides a comprehensive guide for businesses looking to start selling on social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. It outlines the benefits of having a digital presence, offers a 5-step process for establishing business accounts on Facebook and Instagram, and highlights the features of WhatsApp Business for growth. The guide emphasizes content creation, audience interaction, sales opportunities, and performance measurement using platform analytics.

title: Tennessee Valley Authority, Facebook partner on solar farm in Millington
summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) and Facebook are partnering to build a 150-megawatt solar farm in Millington, Tennessee. This project is intended to largely offset the electric demand of a Facebook data center in Gallatin and supports both companies' goals for renewable energy. The solar farm will be built by Germany-based RWE AG and is also seen as a public relations benefit for TVA amid discussions from Memphis's utility about potentially leaving TVA's power supply.

title: T-Mobile entices small businesses with FWA and Facebook marketing
summary: T-Mobile is making a significant push into the small- and medium-sized business (SMB) market by rolling out three new services effective June 1. These include a fixed wireless access (FWA) service called Small Business Internet, new smartphone plans tailored for SMBs, and a "Facebook Advertising on Us" program to assist with digital marketing. The company aims to compete with traditional ISPs by offering FWA without contracts at a competitive price and is also collaborating with Facebook to enhance SMBs' digital marketing capabilities.

title: Vornado nabs Empire Health as tenant for Penn 1 office tower
summary: Vornado Realty Trust has secured a new 70,000-square-foot lease at its Penn 1 office tower with Empire Health Choice, which is relocating from downtown. This deal is part of a larger $450 million capital improvement program for Penn 1, including extensive "WorkLife" amenities. The lease marks a significant win for Vornado's Phase I redevelopment efforts around Penn Station.

title: Facebook Board Rejects Proposals to Curb Zuckerberg’s Power
summary: Facebook's board rejected two proposals aimed at reducing CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control over the company. One proposal sought to replace Zuckerberg as chairman with an independent representative, but the board's decision was anticipated given Zuckerberg controls about 58% of the voting shares. This outcome is a disappointment for those concerned about the extent of his power.

title: Apple Faces Criticism Over Its Cooperation With China
summary: Apple is facing increasing criticism for its cooperation with Chinese laws, which involve sharing consumer data and censoring content, amid a wider technological and economic competition between the U.S. and China. The article also discusses the US Senate's "Endless Frontier Act" aimed at countering China's tech advancements, China's efforts to influence Latin American and African telecom markets, and its crackdown on cryptocurrency and its own tech giants.

title: 'They have clear double standards': T V Mohandas Pai slams large social media platforms
summary: T V Mohandas Pai, former CFO of Infosys, criticized large social media platforms like WhatsApp for having "double standards" regarding user privacy. He stated that the Indian government and laws, not private platforms, should define and protect citizens' privacy. Pai's comments came in response to WhatsApp's lawsuit challenging new Indian digital rules that require the company to provide access to encrypted messages, predicting the issue would reach the Supreme Court.

title: Pride Month meets Wall Street as new LGBTQ ETF hits the market
summary: A new LGBTQ-focused ETF, the LGBTQ100 ESG ETF, has been launched by ProcureAM in partnership with LGBTQ Loyalty Holdings. This fund aims to identify the top 100 companies that align with the LGBTQ community's ESG goals, including companies like Estee Lauder and Facebook. Industry experts believe this ETF will attract attention due to strong advocacy and a new generation of investors who prioritize social governance alongside financial returns, creating a positive feedback loop for companies that embrace diversity.

title: Apple is turning privacy into a business advantage, not just a marketing slogan
summary: Apple is increasingly integrating privacy measures into its products and services, differentiating itself from competitors. Recent announcements include features like email tracking prevention, IP address obfuscation, and burner emails, all under the umbrella of iCloud+. The company leverages its self-designed chips and on-device processing capabilities to enhance privacy and introduce new functionalities in areas like health and digital identity, reinforcing user trust and opening new market opportunities.

title: Six Flags Great America season pass holders could get up to $200 each in $36 million class-action privacy settlement
summary: Six Flags Great America has agreed to a $36 million settlement in a class-action privacy lawsuit concerning the use of fingerprint scanners. Season pass holders and members who visited the park between October 1, 2013, and December 31, 2018, could receive up to $200 each. The lawsuit stemmed from alleged violations of Illinois' biometric privacy law, which does not require proof of actual injury for a claim to proceed.

title: Jessica Ashooh: The taming of Reddit and the National Security State Plant tabbed to do it
summary: The article discusses the controversial appointment of foreign policy hawk Jessica Ashooh as Reddit's Director of Policy in 2017. It highlights her background at the Atlantic Council and the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, detailing her hawkish stances on Middle Eastern foreign policy, particularly regarding Syria. The author suggests her appointment is part of a broader trend of national security state influence over social media platforms, aiming to control content and narratives.

title: New research shows social media has created a more
summary: New research from Sprout Social indicates that social media has intensified competition for brands, with 93% of marketers agreeing, but also serves as a critical tool for differentiation and staying ahead. The 2021 Sprout Social Index: Accelerate highlights that 90% of marketers rely on social data to gain a competitive edge, though few fully leverage this data for ROI measurement or business decisions. The study also reveals that while consumers expect strong customer service on social, marketers often deprioritize it, missing opportunities for engagement and bottom-line growth.

title: Crece las ventas de tu negocio con WhatsApp Business
summary: This article from Bancolombia discusses how businesses can leverage WhatsApp Business to increase sales. It highlights the preference of customers for messenger-based communication over calls or emails, and explains the differences between WhatsApp Consumer, Business, and Business API. The article also provides guidance on setting up a WhatsApp Business profile, utilizing its features like greetings and quick replies, and creating product catalogs to showcase offerings effectively.

title: IAS IPO News - Vista Equity's ad verification platform Integral Ad Science sets terms for $240 million IPO
summary: Integral Ad Science Holding, an ad verification platform backed by Vista Equity, has announced terms for its initial public offering, aiming to raise $240 million. The company, which uses AI and machine learning to verify digital ad performance and brand safety, plans to offer 15 million shares at a price range of $15 to $17. Integral Ad Science booked $254 million in sales for the 12 months ended March 31, 2021, and will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol IAS.

title: Billionaire investor Peter Thiel has $5B in his tax-free retirement account, report finds
summary: A ProPublica report alleges that billionaire investor Peter Thiel grew his Roth IRA to $5 billion, largely tax-free, by investing early shares of PayPal and Facebook. This practice, while legal, raises questions about the effectiveness and fairness of the current tax system, according to tax experts and lawmakers. The report highlights how the wealthy can use retirement accounts, intended for middle-class savings, to accumulate vast, tax-exempt fortunes from capital gains.

title: Antitrust and Platform Monopoly
summary: This article argues that large digital platforms are not "winner-take-all" entities and require competition, making antitrust policy relevant. It suggests that antitrust's firm-specific approach is better suited than broad regulation to address threats to platform competition, particularly when platforms exert market power over other firms. The author proposes remedies beyond breaking up companies, such as restructuring management, requiring interoperability, or mandating information pooling to foster competition and leverage network effects, while also noting that existing merger enforcement tools are inadequate for platform acquisitions of nascent firms.

title: Israel’s Taboola Goes Public Via SPAC At $2.6B Valuation
summary: Israeli content recommendation firm Taboola has gone public on Nasdaq after merging with SPAC ION Acquisition Corp., achieving a valuation of approximately $2.6 billion. Founded in 2007, Taboola partners with over 9,000 digital properties to provide content recommendations and monetization solutions, leveraging AI to deliver over 1 trillion recommendations monthly. The company previously attempted a merger with rival Outbrain in 2019 to challenge Google and Facebook's advertising dominance, but the deal ultimately fell through.

title: 'Abuse of dominance': Was this what Congress originally intended for Section 2?
summary: The article discusses a potential shift in U.S. antitrust enforcement, moving toward stricter policing of single-firm dominance, akin to the European "abuse of dominance" standard. This change is influenced by Senator Amy Klobuchar's proposed legislation and President Biden's appointment of Lina M. Khan to the FTC, reflecting concerns about the market power of technology giants. The author argues that this renewed approach to antitrust law may align more closely with the original intent of the Sherman Act, which historically sought to prevent concentration of power.

title: Trump sues tech firms for blocking him, and fund-raises off it. (Published 2021)
summary: Former President Donald J. Trump sued Facebook, Twitter, and Google, and their CEOs, after being banned or blocked from their platforms. He announced a class-action lawsuit, arguing wrongful censorship and calling it a "very beautiful development," while his political operation immediately began fundraising off the news. Legal experts expressed skepticism about the suit, particularly its arguments that tech firms are "state actors" and that Section 230 is unconstitutional.

title: Trump sues Facebook, Twitter and Google over social media bans
summary: Former US President Donald Trump has filed class-action lawsuits against Facebook, Twitter, and Google, as well as their chief executives, aiming to overturn his social media bans and seek punitive damages. Trump argues that these tech giants, by banning him, are violating First Amendment rights and should be considered government actors due to their liability protections under Section 230. The lawsuits follow his permanent ban from Twitter and a two-year suspension from Facebook after the January 6 Capitol riot, reigniting debates about Section 230 and social media censorship of conservative viewpoints.

title: Trump sues Facebook, Twitter and Google, claiming censorship
summary: Former U.S. President Donald Trump has filed lawsuits against Facebook, Twitter, and Google, along with their chief executives, alleging unlawful censorship of conservative viewpoints. The lawsuits, seeking class action status, claim the social media companies violated First Amendment rights and also ask a judge to invalidate Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act. These legal actions follow the companies' decisions to suspend Trump's accounts after the January 6th Capitol riot, citing violations of policies against glorifying violence.

title: News Corp. closes Knewz aggregator site
summary: News Corp. has shut down its news aggregation service, Knewz, just 18 months after its launch. The platform, which aimed to offer diverse news content as an alternative to Google and Facebook, cited a lack of profitability as the reason for its closure despite attracting millions of users. News Corp. stated that Knewz served as an important proving ground for technology that will continue to benefit its other businesses.

title: Reddit Upvotes The Land Down Under
summary: Reddit has officially launched its Australian operations with a new office in Sydney, recognizing Australia as its fourth-largest user base and a key part of its international growth strategy. The new team includes dedicated Community, Engineering, Sales staff, and Country Manager David Ray, aiming to build on strong organic user growth and establish local brand partnerships. Australian Reddit users are highly engaged, spending more time on the platform than on Instagram, Snapchat, Twitter, and Pinterest, and show popularity for local communities alongside global trends.

title: How VR and AR Can Help You Better Visualize Projects
summary: This article explores how Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) technologies are transforming product visualization for designers, engineers, and clients. It differentiates between VR's immersive 3D environments and AR's superimposed graphics, detailing their real-world applications beyond gaming, such as in product design, education, and simulation. The piece emphasizes the benefits of these technologies in improving the design and review process by allowing interactive previews of products in their intended spaces.

title: Spotify’s Top Lawyer Has Spent Years Making Apple the Bad Guy
summary: Horacio Gutierrez, Spotify’s chief legal officer, has been a key figure in the ongoing antitrust battle against Apple. Having previously defended Microsoft in an antitrust case, Gutierrez has now switched sides and led Spotify's campaign, aiming to portray Apple as an abusive monopolist. His efforts have contributed to a significant shift in public perception regarding Apple's business practices, making it a target for antitrust scrutiny alongside other tech giants.

title: Facebook Users Said No to Tracking. Now Advertisers are Panicking
summary: Facebook advertisers are facing a crisis due to Apple's new iOS privacy features. Users are largely opting out of app tracking, disrupting a key data source for targeted advertising. This shift is leading to decreased ad effectiveness and widespread concern among businesses relying on Facebook's ad platform.

title: SK Telecom enters the metaverse with ifland app
summary: SK Telecom has launched ifland, a new metaverse platform, by upgrading its JUMP Virtual Meetup app. ifland aims to compete with Naver's Zepeto by focusing on communication for users in their 20s and 30s, offering free custom avatars, virtual rooms for voice chats, and various meeting themes. Future updates will include text chats, iOS availability, and online events like concerts.

title: Will DaVita’s indictment alter its big political spending in California?
summary: Dialysis giant DaVita and its former CEO face federal antitrust charges, raising questions about the company's substantial political spending in California. DaVita spent $135 million to defeat two ballot measures and contributed $1.3 million to state politicians, making it a major player in California politics. The indictment, while unrelated to patient treatment, could impact lawmakers' willingness to accept contributions from the company.

title: Kotak Global Innovation Fund of Fund Review
summary: The Kotak Global Innovation Fund of Fund, which invests in the Wellington Global Innovation Fund, is reviewed in this article. The author advises investors to avoid this fund despite its recent outperformance due to high expense ratios and the fund's short history, suggesting alternatives like the Motilal Oswal S&P 500 Index Fund for international market exposure. The fund invests in global companies driving innovation and structural growth trends.

title: Conflict Behind Keller Lenkner Disqualification in Facebook Case
summary: A federal judge disqualified Keller Lenkner as plaintiffs' counsel in a proposed class action lawsuit against Facebook Inc. due to a conflict of interest. The disqualification occurred because a new hire, Albert Pak, had previously represented Facebook in similar antitrust investigations while at Kellogg Hansen. The lawsuit alleges that excessive exposure to Facebook and Instagram causes harm such as suicides, eating disorders, and sleeplessness.

title: How an Investor Helped Netflix Disclose Its ESG Performance
summary: Individual investor Lily Bowles successfully prompted Netflix to disclose its material ESG performance through a shareholder resolution, which she later withdrew after the company demonstrated willingness to comply. Her experience highlights how difficult it is for individual investors to engage with companies, especially with new SEC restrictions that make such efforts harder to replicate despite the potential for positive change. The article also discusses the potential for rule changes under the new SEC chairperson to mitigate these challenges.

title: Apple’s Attack on Email Marketing: Is It Helping Push the Industry Forward?
summary: Apple's introduction of iOS 15 and macOS Monterey Mail Privacy Protection features, including "Mail Privacy Protection" and "Hide My Email," will significantly impact email marketing by limiting marketers' ability to track email opens and user data. These changes, driven by a global push for data privacy following regulations like GDPR and fines against companies like Google and Facebook, compel email marketers to reassess their strategies, move beyond open rates as a primary KPI, and adapt their attribution models. The article suggests that while these privacy enhancements pose challenges, they could ultimately push the email marketing industry toward more efficient and effective practices focused on deeper engagement metrics.

title: The Walt Disney Co. Will Require That Salaried And Non-Union Hourly Employees In U.S. Be Vaccinated
summary: The Walt Disney Co. has announced a new requirement for all salaried and non-union hourly employees in the U.S. to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19. Unvaccinated employees working on site will have 60 days to comply, while new hires will need to be fully vaccinated before starting employment. The company is also discussing the mandate with unions representing its collectively bargained workers, citing health and safety as a top priority.

title: Klarna acquires platform that connects content creators, retailers
summary: Klarna announced its acquisition of Apprl, a platform connecting content creators and retailers, to expand its retail marketing services. This move allows Klarna's partners to collaborate with creators on shoppable content and measure campaign results, aiming to enrich the shopping experience and accelerate retailer growth. The acquisition follows other strategic moves by Klarna, highlighting its entry into social commerce alongside other major companies.

title: American Eagle debuts digital clothing on Bitmoji in creator-focused push
summary: American Eagle is launching its first digital clothing collection on Bitmoji, featuring virtual versions of its brand ambassadors showcasing back-to-school outfits that mirror their appearances in new "Future Together. Jeans Forever" ads. The initiative also includes an augmented reality (AR) experience on Snapchat, allowing users to virtually try on and shop select items. This move reflects American Eagle's strategy to align marketing content with social commerce tools and leverage influencer appeal, especially after successful collaborations with creators like Addison Rae.

title: SoftBank pauses China investing as crackdown roils portfolio
summary: SoftBank Group Corp will pause new investments in China due to regulatory actions against Chinese tech firms, according to CEO Masayoshi Son. Despite the crackdown impacting valuations of previous investments like Didi Global Inc and Full Truck Alliance, SoftBank's Vision Fund CFO Navneet Govil stated that their long-term thesis for China remains unchanged due to its compelling economic opportunity. The fund reported a profit of 236 billion yen in the first quarter, with further upside expected from upcoming listings of Indian firms Paytm and Policybazaar, and Southeast Asian ride-hailer Grab.

title: Unity buys remote desktop streaming app Parsec for $320M, its biggest acquisition yet
summary: Unity Software Inc. is acquiring remote desktop provider Parsec Cloud Inc. for $320 million, marking its largest acquisition to date. This move underscores Unity's ambition to expand beyond video game development and attract more creators to its platform, leveraging Parsec's remote desktop streamlining capabilities for real-time 3D experiences. The acquisition coincides with Unity reporting strong second-quarter financial results, beating Wall Street's expectations with a 48% increase in revenue year-over-year.

title: Class Action Claims Facebook Advertising Platform Allows Scammers to Thrive [UPDATE]
summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that Facebook's advertising platform actively facilitates and encourages scammers to target users with deceptive ads, prioritizing revenue over user safety. An update notes that the initial lawsuit was dismissed with leave to amend, as the judge found Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act immunized Facebook from liability, unless it could be proven Facebook actively developed the illegal ad content. The lawsuit highlights Facebook's alleged involvement at industry conferences attended by known scammers and its turning a blind eye to policy violations from high-paying advertisers, particularly those based in China.

title: Apricot Subsea Cable: Google, Facebook, PLDT, Chunghwa Partner
summary: Google, Facebook, PLDT, Chunghwa Telecom, and NTT Ltd have formed a consortium to build the Apricot subsea cable system, which will span 7,500 miles connecting Singapore, Japan, Taiwan, the Philippines, Indonesia, and Guam. The cable, expected to be operational in 2024 with an initial design capacity of 190+ terabits per second, aims to enhance internet capacity, speed, redundancy, and reliability in the Asia-Pacific region. PLDT is investing $80 million in the project, which will support growing demand for 4G, 5G, broadband, IoT, AI, AR/VR, cloud services, and videoconferencing, and improve digital resilience for all partners.

title: Opinion: Bullish optimism boosting ‘unicorn’ stocks is more like delirium — and a harsh dose of reality is coming
summary: The article argues that the current bullish optimism surrounding "unicorn" stocks is akin to delirium, suggesting that a harsh dose of reality is imminent for these highly valued private companies. It draws a parallel to the early, uncertain stages of now-successful tech giants, highlighting that most "half-baked ideas" fail, and entrepreneurs often operate without hard evidence. The piece implies that the market is overvaluing these companies and that their current high valuations are unsustainable.

title: Apple relying on frequent COVID testing for employees, no vaccine requirement yet
summary: Apple is implementing a strategy of frequent COVID-19 testing for its corporate and retail employees, starting with twice a week and increasing to three times, as it prepares for office reopenings. Unlike some other tech giants, Apple is not currently mandating COVID-19 vaccinations for employees but encourages them for those eligible. The company has also reconsidered restarting in-store classes and plans a hybrid remote work strategy for office staff.

title: SK Telecom talks new virtual world in its metaverse press conference
summary: SK Telecom held the first metaverse press conference in Korea on its new platform, ifland, outlining its vision to expand virtual services globally. The company plans to host various virtual events, recruit "ifluencers" to create and sell in-app items, and intends to support a new virtual economy. ifland, an upgrade to JUMP Virtual Meetup, aims to compete with Naver's Zepeto and will be launched in 80 countries, eventually expanding to PCs and VR devices.

title: Big Tech Is in a Perilous Moment. The Stocks Are Unstoppable.
summary: Despite significant regulatory scrutiny, major tech companies like Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Facebook have demonstrated unstoppable stock performance. During the April to June quarter, these five giants collectively generated $332 billion in revenue, a 36% increase year over year, with all reporting better-than-expected profits. Interestingly, most of their stocks sold off slightly after the positive earnings announcements.

title: Youtube says it has paid out more than $30 billion to online creators
summary: YouTube announced it has paid out over $30 billion to content creators in the past three years through ads, merchandising, and other features. This move comes as competition for online content and creators intensifies from rivals like Facebook, TikTok, and Spotify. YouTube maintains its 45% ad revenue share, emphasizing growing the overall pie for creators.

title: China’s politics in command economy
summary: The Chinese government has been increasingly cracking down on its domestic tech monopolies, including blocking Ant Financial's IPO, banning Didi from app stores, and restricting the for-profit education market. These actions, which have significantly impacted stock values and economic growth, are seen as a deliberate strategy by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) to tighten political control. The CCP aims to balance economic growth with maintaining its power, shifting towards greater state control and self-sufficiency in strategic industries, potentially at the cost of innovation from private enterprises.

title: Will Facebook Stock Ever Split? (NASDAQ:FB)
summary: This article discusses the potential for a stock split for Facebook (FB), noting its attractive growth and valuation. The author suggests that while a stock split could be beneficial for factors like index inclusion, investors should not base their buying decisions solely on this possibility. Facebook is presented as an attractive investment with or without a stock split.

title: Emerson is back in court after judge rejects $77m BladeRoom trade secrets ruling
summary: Emerson Electric has won a new chance to dispute allegations of stealing trade secrets from UK company BladeRoom to build a data center for Facebook, after a previous $77 million ruling was vacated. The 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals found that the district court had misinterpreted a non-disclosure agreement between BladeRoom and Emerson, preventing Emerson from presenting its full defense. The case, which involves allegations of intellectual property theft related to modular data center designs for Facebook's Luleå data center, will now return to court for a new trial.

title: Now Patched Vulnerability in WhatsApp could have led to data exposure of users
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) uncovered a theoretical Out-Of-Bounds read-write vulnerability in WhatsApp related to its image filter functionality. This flaw, patched in version 2.21.1.13, could have allowed an attacker to read sensitive information from WhatsApp's memory following complex user interactions, though WhatsApp found no evidence of its exploitation. The vulnerability stemmed from insufficient checks on image format and size during filter application, leading to out-of-bounds memory access with maliciously crafted image files.

title: Coursera learning platform review
summary: This review evaluates Coursera, an online learning platform specializing in business and computer science courses, highlighting its extensive catalog, partnerships with top universities and corporations, and flexible learning options from free courses to online graduate degrees. While praising its educational offerings and smartphone apps, the review points out areas for improvement such as limited support options, unclear certificate pricing, and some app-related bugs. Overall, Coursera is recommended for those seeking college-level online education.

title: Roundup: More 6 GHz Wi-Fi in the US, Liberty Global upgrades with Plume, more 6 GHz Wi-Fi in Europe, & latest from Plume IQ
summary: This roundup covers significant advancements in Wi-Fi technology and adoption. The FCC is moving closer to authorizing standard power 6 GHz Wi-Fi in the US, with conditional approvals for AFC systems expected to start after November 30. Liberty Global is upgrading millions of European homes with Plume's intelligent Wi-Fi services, and more European countries are greenlighting 6 GHz Wi-Fi operation. Additionally, Plume IQ reports a growing preference for Smart TVs over streaming STBs and the rising trend of 4K video consumption.

title: Carvana CEO’s dad goes on $3.6B stock selling spree, raising eyebrows
summary: Carvana CEO's father, Ernie Garcia II, has sold over $3.6 billion in company stock since October, raising concerns about the family's control over the used car dealership. This selling spree, facilitated by a predetermined plan that was modified twice, follows a period where Garcia II and his son bought shares at "bargain basement" prices during the pandemic, leading to a lawsuit for insider trading. Despite the massive sales, Garcia II still holds a significant stake, with the company's annual report even warning that the Garcia family's interests might not always align with other stockholders.

title: Microsoft (MSFT) Board Approves $60B Share Repurchase Program
summary: Microsoft's board has approved a new $60 billion share repurchase program and increased its quarterly dividend by 11% to 62 cents per share. This move follows a series of similar buyback programs initiated by the company over the past decade, with the latest coming as a previous $40 billion program is nearing its completion. The announcement is particularly noteworthy given recent efforts by Democrats to impose a tax on corporate stock buybacks, a practice that critics argue can artificially inflate stock prices and EPS.

title: With over $5m investment to date, Visionary Media Group wants to create ‘revolutionary experiences for top-tier artists’
summary: Nashville-based Visionary Media Group has secured over $5 million in investment from its parent company, Visionary Private Equity Group (VPEG). The company aims to create revolutionary experiences for top-tier artists and build technological tools, such as the upcoming social distribution platform Evernova, to empower creatives to tell their stories. Founding managing partners Ronald Zamber and Nick Sciorra emphasize their mission to democratize media and provide a platform for all artists and creatives to connect and advance their work.

title: Disney Is Harnessing The Power Of Influencers With Its ‘Disney Creators Lab’
summary: The Walt Disney Company has launched the 'Disney Creators Lab,' an initiative to guide and train 20 existing social media influencers who promote its brand. This program aims to create a more efficient system for integrating creators into Disney's marketing efforts, offering them online courses on branding, merchandising, and content monetization. While Disney does not directly pay participants, the influencers gain skills that can lead to future financial revenue through brand sponsorships.

title: Apple threatened Facebook ban over slavery posts on Instagram
summary: Apple threatened to remove Facebook's products from its App Store in 2019 after a BBC investigation revealed domestic "slaves" were being sold on apps, including Instagram. The Wall Street Journal's "Facebook Files" revealed Facebook took limited action until Apple's threat, despite internal reports showing knowledge of the online slave trade prior to the BBC's inquiry. Following the BBC report and Apple's intervention, Facebook banned hashtags, removed accounts, and developed technology to proactively address content related to domestic servitude.

title: Apple’s power move to kneecap Facebook advertising is working
summary: Apple's iOS 14.5 privacy changes, which allow users to opt-out of app tracking, are significantly harming Facebook's advertising business. Advertisers, particularly performance marketers, are struggling to measure ad effectiveness and are consequently reducing their spending on Facebook and diversifying to other platforms like Snapchat, TikTok, and email. Critics suggest Apple's move is not solely privacy-driven but also a strategic play to build its own advertising platform, as it competes directly with Facebook's messaging apps.

title: Brain-science products roll out despite ethical, validity concerns
summary: Japanese companies are increasing their research into "brain technology," developing products for marketing, health, and concentration, some of which are already on the market. However, significant ethical and validity concerns persist, as many products lack robust scientific evidence and questions arise about the intrusiveness of technologies that delve into human brain activities. Experts are working to establish frameworks to assess the trustworthiness of these products to build public confidence and guide industry development.

title: Etsy debuts shoppable virtual house
summary: Etsy has launched "Etsy House," an interactive augmented reality experience allowing shoppers to tour a digital home decorated with marketplace items. This initiative builds on Etsy's previous AR offerings and positions it alongside other retailers like David's Bridal, Asos, and Amazon, who are utilizing AR and VR to enhance product visualization and e-commerce. The company has also recently expanded its business through acquisitions of Depop and Elo7.

title: INSIGHTS | Conservative investors are pairing portfolio with principles
summary: Tom Carter, a mutual fund executive, has launched the American Conservative Values ETF to allow conservative investors to align their portfolios with their principles, avoiding "woke" companies. The fund, which began in October and already manages over $28 million, aims to provide an option for individuals who wish to invest in companies that share their conservative values rather than those that engage in social and racial justice advocacy. This initiative reflects a broader movement where conservatives are using economic choices to "fight back" against companies perceived as aligning with liberal politics.

title: WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram back online after hours of outage
summary: WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram were restored after a widespread global outage. The outage, which affected millions of users, caused Facebook shares to fall significantly and led to apologies from the companies involved. The article also mentions previous outages and the potential cause related to DNS errors.

title: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp hit by global outage
summary: Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp experienced a global outage, with the social media giant working to restore services. Experts believe a configuration error or internal mistake might have triggered the outage, causing Facebook's shares to fall by 5.5%. This incident follows previous outages and occurs just a day after a whistleblower accused Facebook of prioritizing profit over addressing hate speech and misinformation.

title: Amazon's Twitch blames configuration error for data breach
summary: Amazon's Twitch has attributed a recent data breach to an error in a server configuration change, which allowed an alleged hacker to leak sensitive information. The platform is still assessing the full impact but has reset all stream keys, while assuring users that login credentials and full credit card details were not exposed. This incident follows a similar "faulty configuration change" that caused a widespread outage for Facebook Inc.

title: Facebook Changes and Second Whistleblower, Comcast’s Spam Call Feature, AT&T Picks Ericsson for 5G
summary: Facebook is implementing changes to protect teens from harmful content on Instagram and is facing a second whistleblower. Comcast has launched a new spam call blocking feature for its Xfinity Voice customers, allowing them to manage unwanted calls. AT&T has partnered with Ericsson in a five-year deal to build out its standalone 5G network using C-band spectrum, aiming to cover a significant portion of the U.S. population by the end of 2023.

title: Tesla's Growing Investor Revolt
summary: Despite a significant increase in its stock price, Tesla is facing a growing investor revolt concerning its corporate governance, including diversity initiatives, employee relations, and board structure. Shareholder resolutions addressing these issues gained substantial support, with several nearly passing if not for Elon Musk's controlling stake. This trend signals increasing dissatisfaction among shareholders who are scrutinizing the company's management beyond just financial performance.

title: Trump to launch new social media platform TRUTH Social
summary: Former US President Donald Trump has announced the creation of a new social media network called TRUTH Social, aiming to "stand up to the tyranny of big tech" after his bans from Twitter and Facebook. An early version will launch next month for invited guests, with a full rollout expected in early 2022. The platform is intended to be a rival to existing social media giants, despite skepticism about its reach and overtly politicized nature.

title: Trump wants his media company to rival Twitter, Netflix and Amazon
summary: Former President Donald Trump announced the launch of Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), aiming to create a media network that rivals Big Tech platforms like Twitter, Netflix, and Amazon. The company plans to launch a social media site called TRUTH Social, develop a subscription video-on-demand service (TMTG+), and build internet technology infrastructure. This initiative comes after Trump's bans from major social media platforms and saw TMTG's stock surge over 350% on its debut through a merger with Digital World Acquisition Corp.

title: Facebook’s reported name change reinforces its image as the new Big Tobacco
summary: Facebook is reportedly planning to rebrand itself with a new name, drawing comparisons to Philip Morris's name change to Altria Group two decades ago. Critics argue that a new brand name won't solve Facebook's fundamental problems, such as the negative effects of its platforms and its tendency to prioritize profit over public health, echoing sentiments that Big Tobacco used rebranding to distract from harmful practices. Experts suggest that for the rebrand to be successful, it needs to be accompanied by a genuine internal change in culture, values, and vision, rather than just a superficial PR move.

title: Snap tumbles, drags social media giants on Apple privacy tweak worries
summary: Snap's shares plunged by nearly 20% after the company warned that Apple's new iOS privacy changes would have a prolonged negative impact on its advertising revenue, also dragging down other ad-dependent tech firms like Facebook, Google, and Twitter. Analysts cut Snap's price targets, expecting the impact to last into next year. The company cited global supply chain disruptions and labor shortages as additional factors compounding the advertising slowdown.

title: Why Unity Software's Business Model Has Market-Beating Upside Built In
summary: Unity Software's business model, particularly its usage-based "Operate" segment, offers significant upside potential as it profits directly from the success of its creators. The company provides its creation tools free to smaller developers, attracting a broad user base and benefiting immensely when their games become hits. Analysts highlight Unity's expanding market beyond gaming into verticals like architecture and film, and its strategic advantage over competitors like Unreal Engine due to its ease of use.

title: From pushback on Facebook's digital wallet to iris scanning for free coins: 6 things that happened in crypto this past week
summary: This article summarizes six key developments in the crypto space from the past week, including Bitcoin and Ether reaching new all-time highs. Other significant events include the launch of the first U.S. futures-based bitcoin ETF, senators' pushback against Facebook's Novi digital wallet project, Worldcoin's iris-scanning-for-crypto initiative, Robinhood's crypto wallet waitlist exceeding 1 million users, Mastercard's move to allow crypto services on its network, and Nigeria's central bank digital currency going live.

title: Men Taking 6 Months Parental Leave Are ‘Losers,’ Top VC Says
summary: Joe Lonsdale, a prominent venture capitalist and Palantir co-founder, stirred controversy by calling men who take six months of parental leave "losers" in response to criticism directed at Pete Buttigieg. This sparked a strong backlash, with other venture capitalists like Alexis Ohanian and Garry Tan defending their four-month parental leave policies. Lonsdale later walked back the use of the word "loser" but reiterated his stance on traditional gender roles.

title: Facebook changing its corporate name to Meta as part of rebrand
summary: Facebook Inc. has officially rebranded to Meta Platforms Inc., or Meta, reflecting CEO Mark Zuckerberg's new focus on the "metaverse." While the social network retains its original name, the corporate change aims to emphasize the company's commitment to developing immersive virtual environments. This rebranding occurs amid intense scrutiny and criticism following the "Facebook Papers" leaks, with skeptics suggesting it's an attempt to divert attention from the company's ongoing controversies.

title: Facebook wants to lean into the metaverse. Here's what it is and how it will work
summary: Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced that the company is rebranding to Meta Platforms Inc., signaling a major shift towards the metaverse. The metaverse is envisioned as a network of interconnected virtual communities where people can interact, work, and play using VR/AR devices. Other major tech companies and game developers are also investing in this concept, but concerns remain about data privacy and the potential for increased online harms if social media giants like Facebook carry their current business models into this new virtual frontier.

title: Facebook’s new Meta watch to rival Apple is leaked online
summary: An image of a potential Meta (formerly Facebook) smartwatch, reportedly designed to compete with the Apple Watch, has been leaked online. The watch, if it comes to market, features a front-facing camera, a rounded screen, and a heart-rate monitor, aiming to differentiate itself from existing smartwatches. Meta is said to be working on multiple generations of the product with a possible launch in early 2022.

title: What Does Facebook, Inc.’s Name Change Really Mean?
summary: Facebook, Inc. rebranded to Meta amidst speculation and efforts to pivot to the metaverse, following a trend of companies changing names to reflect expansion or reposition brands. While some view such changes as primarily semantic, branding experts suggest they can make sense from a brand architecture standpoint and signal broader strategic shifts. The article highlights how similar rebrands by companies like Michael Kors (Capri Holdings) and Coach (Tapestry) were accompanied by significant internal changes and strategic pushes upmarket, suggesting Meta's success will depend on similar substantive transformations.

title: Facebook Announces Corporate Name Change to Meta
summary: Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the company's corporate name change to Meta Platforms Inc., aligning with its focus on developing the metaverse. The rebrand positions the company as a computing platform, moving beyond its social media-first identity, despite ongoing controversies surrounding data privacy and content moderation. The company's main social media apps will retain their names, and its stock will trade under the new ticker MVRS starting December 1st.

title: Danforth: When in doubt, rebrand
summary: The article discusses Facebook's decision to rebrand as Meta Platforms, Inc., following controversies surrounding misinformation and whistleblower Frances Haugen's revelations. The author, Dave Danforth, suggests this rebranding is a tactic to distance the company from negative associations, akin to previous corporate name changes like Altria (formerly Phillip Morris) or AirTran (formerly ValuJet). He also touches on Mark Zuckerberg's continued control over the company due to unique stock ownership and questions the board's oversight.

title: Trump's Truth Social platform could make millions — or go bust
summary: Donald Trump is launching a new social media site, Truth Social, which aims to challenge Big Tech and provide him with a digital presence after being banned from major platforms. While Trump portrays the venture as "saving our country," it also has a significant financial aspect, with the potential to make millions or fail, given his past business track record. The platform will operate via a SPAC merger with Digital World Acquisition Corp. (DWAC) and faces questions regarding its financial viability and ability to attract sustained user engagement and advertising revenue.

title: Pinterest Announces ‘Pinterest TV’ Shoppable Live-Stream Series
summary: Pinterest is launching "Pinterest TV," a new series of shoppable live-stream events beginning November 8th, to capitalize on the growing live commerce trend. These daily episodes will feature creators, exclusive deals from brands, and interactive chat functions. The platform is also creating a virtual studio to help more creators produce their own live shopping streams within the app, further boosting its e-commerce focus.

title: Meta denies Kazakh claim of exclusive access to Facebook's content reporting system
summary: Meta Platforms has denied claims by the Kazakh government that it had been granted exclusive access to Facebook's content reporting system. Kazakhstan had announced the purported agreement as a compromise to avoid a potential block of Facebook for millions of local users. Meta clarified that it has a consistent global process for governments to report content violating local laws, which is uniform across all countries.

title: Facebook to shut down facial recognition system, delete face prints of 1 billion users
summary: Facebook has announced it will shut down its facial recognition system and delete the face prints of over a billion users due to growing concerns about the technology's misuse and increasing regulatory scrutiny. This move, described as one of the largest shifts in facial recognition use, comes amidst a crisis for Facebook (now Meta) and follows years of criticism regarding privacy and the ethics of such technology. While the company stated this specific broad identification method would cease, it did not rule out using facial recognition for narrower authentication purposes in future products, particularly for on-device applications.

title: Microsoft reveals its metaverse ambitions by presenting virtual platform Mesh
summary: Microsoft unveiled its plans to integrate metaverse capabilities into its Teams platform with the launch of Mesh. This new platform will enable users to create 3D avatars for virtual meetings and immersive experiences, without requiring VR headsets. Microsoft also aims to bring its metaverse ambitions to gaming, seeing titles like Halo and Minecraft as foundational to this vision.

title: B. Riley Named “Fastest Growing Company” by Fortune
summary: B. Riley (RILY) has been named the second fastest-growing company overall by Fortune, with its banking and wealth management businesses driving significant revenue and earnings per share growth. Financial service companies dominated this year's list, surpassing technology firms. The company attributes part of its success to its ability to attract and retain high-achieving talent.

title: Facebook will shut down facial recognition system
summary: Facebook announced it is shutting down its facial recognition system due to growing societal concerns and regulatory uncertainty regarding the technology's use. This move will delete the facial recognition templates of over 1 billion people and comes amid increased scrutiny on the tech industry's ethical use of such systems. While privacy groups welcome the decision, Facebook has not ruled out using facial recognition in other limited use cases like identity verification.

title: Facebook to shut down face-recognition system, delete data
summary: Facebook plans to shut down its decade-old facial recognition system this month, deleting the face scan data of over one billion users. This move comes amid growing privacy concerns, government investigations, and regulatory pressure. The company, now under its new parent name Meta, aims to transition towards narrower forms of personal authentication.

title: As pandemic home life eases, EA should reach into the Metaverse
summary: Analysts suggest that as pandemic home life eases, Electronic Arts Inc. should develop a metaverse strategy around its popular game titles to keep players engaged and drive further monetization. This move is seen as crucial for video game publishers to stay relevant in the long haul, especially as the global metaverse market is projected to grow significantly. EA is currently reviewing its naming rights agreement with FIFA and faces competition from rivals like Roblox and Epic Games' Fortnite, which already incorporate metaverse elements.

title: Investing in Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of the Metaverse with an ETF
summary: This article discusses investing in Mark Zuckerberg's vision of the Metaverse following Facebook's rebranding to Meta. It explains what the Metaverse is, how investors can gain exposure through companies involved in its creation like Roblox and Unity Software, and highlights the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (NYSE:META) which tracks a basket of such stocks. The article also provides information on thematic ETFs and the fund manager, Roundhill Investments.

title: How To Target Your Audience Without Third-Party Cookie Data
summary: This article explores the impending demise of third-party cookies by late 2023 and its implications for digital advertising. It discusses how advertisers will face challenges in targeting ads and measuring performance, and outlines three potential scenarios for digital ad targeting: walled gardens, a consent economy, and identity innovation. The article also provides strategies for marketers to adapt, focusing on first-party data, direct publisher relationships, and contextual advertising.

title: EXPLAINED: What is Metaverse and Why Facebook/ Meta Thinks it's the Future of Internet
summary: This article explains the concept of the metaverse, why Facebook (now Meta) views it as the future of the internet, and what its potential applications are. It details how the metaverse would work, from virtual interactions and business opportunities to the technologies being developed to build it, while also touching on data privacy concerns.

title: AMD shares close up 10% after company wins Meta partnership, announces new chips
summary: AMD shares surged 10% after the company announced a partnership with Meta (formerly Facebook) as a chip customer and unveiled a new range of chips at its Accelerated Data Center Premiere event. This move strengthens AMD's position against competitors like Intel, as the company continues to gain market share with its data center chip sales experiencing significant growth. Additional details about the Meta partnership are expected to be revealed later in the week at the Open Compute Project summit.

title: The World’s Cryptocurrency Is Now Worth More Than $3 Trillion
summary: The cryptocurrency market has surpassed a $3 trillion valuation, quadrupling its 2020 year-end value. This growth is attributed to increased investor comfort with established tokens like Bitcoin and Ethereum, advancements in decentralized finance and NFTs, and the rise of memecoins. Despite its notorious volatility, recent rallies in Bitcoin and Ether propelled the market to new highs, with Bitcoin nearing its previous record and Ether reaching a new peak.

title: AMD lands Meta as customer and takes on Nvidia, sending shares up 11%
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares rose 11% after announcing Meta Platforms Inc. as a new data center chip customer, intensifying its competition with Intel. AMD also unveiled new chips, including the MI200 for AI and machine learning to challenge Nvidia, and the Bergamo processor for cloud computing to compete with Ampere Computing. These strategic moves bolster AMD's market position against larger rivals and secure its presence with major cloud providers.

title: Cisco and Meta Partner on Wedge400C Data Center Switch
summary: Cisco and Meta (formerly Facebook) have partnered to deploy Cisco's Silicon One Q200L device in Meta's Wedge400C Top of Rack (TOR) switch. This collaboration signifies Cisco's evolution into a disaggregated consumption model for the open-source community, offering its silicon technology to external customers. The partnership involved extensive design and software integration work, enabling Meta to build a system using Cisco Silicon One running their FBOSS operating system.

title: Meta Stitches Cisco, Arista to Open Compute Project Switches
summary: Meta has integrated Cisco and Arista Networks into its Open Compute Project (OCP) efforts by announcing new top-of-rack switches and improvements to its data center fabrics. This expansion includes the introduction of the OCP Switch Abstraction Interface (SAI) to standardize APIs for network hardware. Meta also shared future goals, including an open die-to-die interface and a commitment to net-zero emissions by 2030.

title: Google loses challenge against EU antitrust ruling, $2.8-bln fine
summary: Alphabet's Google unit lost an appeal against a 2.42-billion-euro ($2.8-billion) antitrust decision by the EU related to its price comparison shopping service. This ruling marks a significant win for Europe's competition chief, Margrethe Vestager, and could strengthen the EU's position in ongoing investigations into other major tech companies like Amazon, Apple, and Facebook. Google stated it would review the judgment and has already complied with the Commission's order to ensure a level playing field.

title: AMD wins Meta as a data centre customer
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) has secured Meta (formerly Facebook) as a data centre chip customer, leading to an 11% surge in AMD's shares. This win highlights AMD's growing market presence against competitors like Nvidia and Intel, especially with the launch of new chips like the MI200 for AI and machine learning, and "Bergamo" for cloud computing. The deal adds Meta to AMD's list of major clients, which already includes Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft Azure.

title: Facebook Is Under Fire, but It's Also Undervalued
summary: Despite ongoing controversies, regulatory scrutiny, and a company name change to Meta Platforms, Morningstar's analysis suggests that the stock is undervalued, trading at a 16% discount to its fair value estimate. The article highlights Meta's two business segments—its legacy apps and the new Reality Labs for metaverse development—and discusses the potential impacts of regulatory and antitrust risks, concluding that the stock remains the most attractive social-media play in Morningstar's coverage. The company's revenue growth is primarily driven by advertising, leveraging its vast user base and the shift towards online spending, while its wide economic moat is based on network effects and intangible data assets.

title: Cisco and SONiC
summary: Cisco is actively supporting SONiC, an open-source operating system for cloud-scale data center networks, by integrating it with their Cisco 8000 series routing platforms. This commitment allows hyperscalers to leverage open capabilities and advanced hardware platforms for their network architectures. Cisco demonstrated their SONiC integration at the 2021 OCP Global Summit and also collaborated with Meta on the Wedge400C data center switch, highlighting their versatile offerings for various customer needs.

title: Nvidia CEO: The metaverse will be 'much, much bigger than the physical world'
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes the metaverse will far surpass the physical world in scale and economic activity. He envisions an internet where virtual creations and training for AI and robotics will be significantly larger than real-world counterparts. Nvidia's Omniverse platform is central to this vision, enabling businesses to create digital twins for various applications, including 5G network layout and autonomous driving simulation.

title: Podcast: Rivian's blockbuster IPO is a triumph of entrepreneurship
summary: This podcast episode discusses Rivian's blockbuster $12 billion IPO, highlighting it as a significant entrepreneurial achievement. It also touches on whether a deal with Meta could help AMD compete more effectively with Intel. The article celebrates Rivian's success and explores potential shifts in the tech industry.

title: Unity launches ‘metaverse’ platforms to simulate robot deployments
summary: Unity has introduced two new products, Unity Simulation Pro and Unity SystemGraph, designed to simulate AI and robotics deployments for virtual testing and analysis. These platforms allow engineers to emulate robotics systems and sensors, and test them at accelerated rates, significantly reducing costs and development time. The move aligns with Unity's pivot from video game engines to enterprise 3D tools and an "industrial metaverse" concept, with real-world applications shown by collaborations with the Allen Institute of AI, Carnegie Mellon University, and Volvo.
