title: Ohio PERS sues Facebook over alleged misrepresentations
summary: The Ohio Public Employees’ Retirement System has filed a securities class-action lawsuit against Meta Platforms Inc. (formerly Facebook) and its executive officers, including CEO Mark Zuckerberg. The lawsuit alleges misrepresentations made by the social media giant. This action comes amidst other financial news concerning private credit, university endowments, and pension funds.

title: Qualcomm forecasts post-Apple sales growth, shares hit all-time high
summary: Qualcomm Inc. expects its chip sales to Apple Inc. to significantly decrease in the coming years as Apple develops its own modem chips. However, Qualcomm anticipates robust growth in other sectors like autonomous cars, the internet of things, and virtual reality headsets, which led to its shares hitting a record high. The company projects substantial revenue increases from automotive and IoT divisions, offsetting the expected decline from Apple.

title: Facebook, Now ‘Meta,’ Accused of Exploiting Children in Lawsuit Lodged by Ohio AG
summary: Ohio Attorney General David Yost has filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms Inc. (formerly Facebook), alleging that the company knowingly exploited children to drive corporate profits. The lawsuit, filed on behalf of the Ohio Public Employees Retirement System, claims Facebook misrepresented its products' safety for children and ignored internal warnings about harmful content. This legal action follows recent revelations from whistleblower Frances Haugen regarding Facebook's awareness of its platforms' negative impact on users, especially children.

title: Luxury NFT Market Could Hit $56B by 2030: Morgan Stanley
summary: Morgan Stanley predicts that the luxury market could generate $56 billion in revenue by 2030 from metaverse gaming and non-fungible tokens (NFTs). The report highlights that NFTs and social gaming offer significant opportunities for luxury brands to monetize their intellectual property. The total NFT market is projected to grow to around $300 billion by 2030, with luxury brands potentially expanding their total addressable market by over 10% and industry earnings by approximately 25%.

title: Apple sues company known for hacking iPhones on behalf of governments
summary: Apple has filed a lawsuit against NSO Group, an Israeli firm that develops software to hack iPhones, alleging that the company weaponizes powerful state-sponsored spyware against innocent users. Apple seeks a permanent injunction to prevent NSO Group from using its software, services, or devices and is seeking damages exceeding $75,000. Additionally, Apple will donate $10 million and any lawsuit damages to organizations combating digital surveillance, while also pledging to inform iPhone users targeted by Pegasus malware.

title: Publicis Groupe's Zenith Wins Eli Lilly U.S. Media Business
summary: Publicis Groupe's Zenith has won the U.S. media business for pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly, following a review process managed by MediaLink that began in June. This significant win adds to a series of recent account successes for Publicis Groupe, including Meta and Walmart's media business. The incumbent, Omnicom's OMD, had held the Eli Lilly business for nearly two decades.

title: Samsung, Hynix notch best day this year; metaverse to drive chip demand
summary: Shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, South Korea's largest chipmakers, experienced their biggest single-day gains this year amid an improving outlook for the memory chip industry. Analysts suggest the current downturn in the memory market could be shorter than expected, driven by the emerging demand from the metaverse. Foreign investors, who had been selling off shares due to pessimistic views, are now returning, further bolstering the stock performance.

title: Meta Postpones Ticker Symbol Change to Q1 2022
summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. announced a postponement of its Class A common stock ticker symbol change until Q1 2022. The company previously intended for the change to be effective on December 1, 2021. In the interim, Meta's Class A common stock will continue to trade on NASDAQ under the ticker symbol 'FB'.

title: Brands No Longer See Metaverse-Like Worlds as Abstract Gimmicks
summary: Major brands like Chipotle, Vans, and Verizon are increasingly engaging with metaverse-like platforms such as Roblox and Fortnite Creative. This strategic move aims to boost brand recognition and deepen customer engagement, indicating that companies are now taking these digital worlds more seriously, especially after Facebook's rebranding brought the metaverse into mainstream awareness.

title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Labaton Sucharow Notifies Meta Platforms, Inc. f/k/a Facebook, Inc. Investors of a Securities Class Action Lawsuit - FB
summary: Labaton Sucharow has filed a class action lawsuit against Facebook, Inc. (now Meta Platforms, Inc.) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between November 3, 2016, and October 4, 2021. The lawsuit alleges that Facebook made false and misleading statements regarding user growth, duplicate accounts, platform fairness, and its handling of illicit activities and attraction of preteens. Investors who suffered losses and wish to serve as lead plaintiff must contact Labaton Sucharow by December 27, 2021.

title: Bret Taylor appointed co-CEO of Salesforce as shares drop on lower-than-expected forcecast
summary: Bret Taylor has been appointed co-chief executive officer of Salesforce Inc. The announcement came the same day Salesforce's shares dropped in after-hours trading due to a lower-than-expected earnings forecast. Despite better-than-expected Q3 results of $1.27 a share profit and $6.86 billion in revenue, investors reacted negatively to Q4 guidance that projected lower profits than analysts anticipated.

title: Facebook parent grabs another 1M sf in Bay Area
summary: Meta (Facebook's parent company) has leased an additional 1 million square feet of office space in the Bay Area, specifically in Sunnyvale and Burlingame, to reduce employee commute times and support its net-zero carbon emission goal. The lease of four buildings in Sunnyvale, totaling over 700,000 square feet, is considered the largest private-sector office lease in the U.S. this year. This expansion further solidifies Sunnyvale's position as a key office market in Silicon Valley.

title: Meta Selects AWS as Key, Long-Term Strategic Cloud Provider
summary: Meta has deepened its relationship with Amazon Web Services (AWS) as a strategic cloud provider, leveraging AWS's infrastructure for research and development, third-party collaborations, and operational efficiency. The companies will also work together to optimize PyTorch performance on AWS, facilitating faster and easier development, training, deploying, and operating of AI/ML models for enterprises. This collaboration aims to help organizations bring large-scale deep learning models from research to production more efficiently on AWS.

title: From Square to Block: Another tech company changes its name
summary: Payments company Square Inc., led by former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey, has changed its name to Block Inc. The rebranding aims to differentiate the corporate entity from its expanding businesses, which now include Tidal, Cash App, and a Bitcoin-focused financial services platform called TBD54566975. The change follows Dorsey's recent resignation as Twitter CEO and reflects the company's growth beyond its original commerce and payments offerings.

title: Meta Directed to Sell Giphy; WPP Acquires Cloud Commerce Group
summary: Meta has been directed by the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) to sell Giphy, following concerns that the acquisition would reduce competition among social media platforms and in the display advertising market. Separately, WPP announced its acquisition of e-commerce technology provider Cloud Commerce Group as part of its strategy to bolster its commerce and technology units. Additionally, Algerian on-demand services provider Yassir raised USD$30m in Series A funding to develop a super-app for the MENA region, focusing on financial inclusion.

title: Meta leases former NetApp HQ in biggest U.S. real estate deal of 2021
summary: Social media giant Meta has leased a more than 700,000-square-foot campus in Sunnyvale, which was formerly NetApp's headquarters. This deal marks the biggest U.S. real estate transaction of 2021. NetApp had been selling off its properties in Sunnyvale since 2016, completing the sale of its final pieces in 2021.

title: Welcome to the Tinderverse: Tinder's CEO talks metaverse, virtual currency
summary: Tinder CEO Renate Nyborg discussed the dating app's exploration of blurring online and offline worlds, coining the term "Tinderverse" during an interview at the Reuters Next conference. The company is testing in-app currency for premium services and rewards, and while acknowledging the metaverse, Nyborg emphasized Tinder's continued focus on facilitating real-life connections, despite the rise of digital interactions during the pandemic.

title: USPTO enlists McGruff the Crime Dog; Lululemon fires back at Peloton; TMview reaches 100 million trademarks – news digest
summary: This news digest covers several key developments in the trademark sphere, including Lululemon's patent infringement lawsuit against Peloton, Japanese Zoom Corp's trademark suit against Zoom Video Communications, and Edgewell's acquisition of Billie. It also highlights the USPTO's anti-counterfeiting campaign with McGruff the Crime Dog and the EUIPO's TMview tool reaching 100 million searchable trademarks, alongside various updates on IP management, brand partnerships, and legal appointments.

title: The metaverse needs aggressive regulation
summary: The author, a pioneer in AR/VR technology, argues for aggressive regulation of the metaverse to prevent large corporations from extensive monitoring and manipulation of users. He emphasizes the need to restrict data collection, regulate real-time marketing tactics, and ensure transparency regarding AI-controlled agents and targeted placements. The article warns that without regulation, the metaverse risks becoming an environment where powerful entities exploit user data and emotions for commercial gain.

title: Trump's social media deal is being investigated by regulators
summary: Regulators, including the SEC, are investigating a planned merger between Digital World Acquisition Corp. (DWAC) and former President Donald Trump's social media startup, Trump Media & Technology Group. DWAC, a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), disclosed on Monday that it is cooperating with "preliminary, fact-finding inquiries" from regulatory authorities. This investigation follows reports that DWAC and the Trump company might have held talks before DWAC went public, which could violate SPAC rules.

title: Rohingya refugees from Myanmar sue Facebook for $150B for spreading hate speech
summary: Rohingya refugees from Myanmar are suing Meta Platforms Inc (formerly Facebook) for $150 billion, alleging the social media company failed to act against anti-Rohingya hate speech that contributed to real-world violence. A class-action lawsuit filed in California and a letter of notice in London claim Facebook's content policing failures and platform design fueled the atrocities. Legal experts note the challenge of applying foreign law in U.S. courts due to Section 230 protections, which shield platforms from liability for user-posted content.

title: Shachar Scott Joins Meta Reality Labs as Director of Brand & International Marketing
summary: Shachar Scott has been appointed as the Director of Brand and International Marketing at Meta Reality Labs, joining on December 6th, 2021. In this role, she will oversee global marketing, creative, media, and production, reporting to Brian Irving. Scott brings extensive experience from previous positions at Bumble, Snapchat, and Apple, where she focused on building and scaling global brands.

title: Department of Justice announces settlement with Microsoft over immigration discrimination claims
summary: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) has settled with Microsoft Corporation regarding claims of discrimination against non-US citizen employees, including lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees. Microsoft was found to have unlawfully required these individuals to prove a need for visa sponsorship and to provide unnecessary work authorization documents. As part of the settlement, Microsoft will reform its hiring processes, pay civil penalties, and be subject to monitoring.

title: Walmart, Nike, and other giant employers aim to cut algorithmic bias from the hiring process
summary: Large companies like Walmart, Nike, and Meta have formed the Data & Trust Alliance to combat algorithmic bias in their hiring processes. This alliance, co-founded by former American Express and IBM CEOs, has developed a toolkit with 55 questions to evaluate AI hiring software and identify unintended discrimination. Their goal is to ensure fair hiring practices and address concerns about AI's potential to perpetuate biases based on past applicant data.

title: Rohingya refugees sue Facebook for $150 billion over Myanmar violence
summary: Rohingya refugees are suing Meta Platforms Inc (formerly Facebook) for $150 billion, alleging the company failed to address anti-Rohingya hate speech on its platform that contributed to violence in Myanmar. Both a U.S. class-action complaint and a letter of notice in the UK have been filed, citing Facebook's inaction and platform design as factors enabling real-world harm. The lawsuit also references previous UN investigations, Reuters reports, and whistleblower claims regarding Facebook's inadequate policing of abusive content in vulnerable countries.

title: Adobe buys social media marketing startup ContentCal
summary: Adobe Inc. has acquired ContentCal, a six-year-old social media marketing startup, for an undisclosed sum reported to be over $100 million. ContentCal’s platform helps businesses manage social marketing planning and processes, offering tools for collaboration, scheduling, and performance tracking. This acquisition is expected to enhance Adobe's creative tools with expanded social media capabilities, following its earlier purchase of Frame.io Inc.

title: Herramientas de redes sociales para el sector servicios
summary: This article from Bancolombia discusses how businesses in the service sector can leverage social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp Business to expand their reach and customer base. It highlights two key e-commerce trends: customers actively searching for products and products "discovering" customers through social media feeds. The piece also provides a step-by-step guide on creating effective advertising campaigns on these platforms, focusing on defining objectives, choosing ad types (forms, calls, messages), and targeting specific audiences.

title: How new office may help Meta widen presence, rebuild image
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. inaugurated its first standalone office in Asia, located in Gurgaon, to house teams for Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. This move is aimed at widening its presence in India, its largest market by users, and rebuilding its image after facing global allegations regarding hate-speech and inadequate local language investment. The new office includes a Centre for Fuelling India’s New Economy (CFINE) designed to train small businesses, entrepreneurs, and creators.

title: Instagram and the mental load of fitness and exercise for women
summary: This article discusses the mental load of fitness and exercise for women, greatly amplified by social media and "fitfluencers." It explores how constant exposure to idealized body images and complex workout regimes can be harmful, leading to added stress and unrealistic expectations. The piece emphasizes the importance of a balanced view on exercise and highlights that real health benefits come from consistent, moderate physical activity rather than extreme ideals.

title: Go With GINN as High-Margin Companies Remain Trendy
summary: Investors are expected to favor quality, high-margin companies in 2022, a trend supported by the Goldman Sachs Innovate Equity ETF (GINN). GINN tracks companies with robust profitability, strong earnings growth, and effective margin management, aligning with Goldman Sachs' recommendation for clients. Several of GINN's holdings, including Alphabet, Meta Platforms, Apple, Marvell Technology, Mastercard, PayPal, Autodesk, and Etsy, are featured on Goldman's list of high-margin companies.

title: Jayhawk Wind Farm in Kansas Commences Commercial Operations
summary: WEC Energy Group's 190 MW Jayhawk Wind Farm in Kansas has begun commercial operations, selling energy to Meta under a long-term contract. WEC Energy Group invested an estimated $302 million for a 90% ownership stake and tax benefits, aligning with its ESG Progress Plan. Invenergy acquired the remaining 10% and will operate the facility, which was developed by Apex Clean Energy.

title: What Zoom’s $85m class action lawsuit means for data privacy
summary: Zoom has agreed to pay an $85 million settlement in a class action lawsuit alleging it shared user data without consent and falsely claimed end-to-end encryption. This case highlights a broader data privacy movement forcing companies to increase transparency and adjust to stricter regulations. Experts believe the lawsuit serves as a cautionary tale for the digital ecosystem and will prompt other companies to re-evaluate their data protection policies.

title: Before the Billions: The First Jobs of Some of the Richest Men in the World
summary: This article explores the humble beginnings of some of the world's wealthiest individuals, highlighting their first jobs before achieving billionaire status. It details the early career paths of 15 billionaires, from Travis Kalanick selling knives door-to-door to Jeff Bezos working as a McDonald's fry cook, demonstrating that even the richest people started with ordinary or unconventional jobs. The piece also includes advice on how readers can work towards boosting their own net worth.

title: The Invesco QQQ Stock Price Is Up 23.7% Since January. Could There Be More Gains?
summary: The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ: QQQ) has seen its stock price rise 23.7% since January, driven by major tech companies like Apple and Google, despite recent pullbacks. Investors are closely watching the Federal Reserve's monetary policy meeting for potential hawkish policies that could further impact the Nasdaq index and the QQQ ETF. While the ETF is currently in a downtrend, its present stock price may be attractive for a future rally, though a clear upward trend based on EMA crossings is yet to materialize.

title: Meta, CBSE tie-up: ‘Opportunity to invest in entrepreneurial spirit,’ says Mark Zuckerberg
summary: Mark Zuckerberg announced an expanded collaboration between Meta and CBSE to train 10 lakh teachers and over a crore students in virtual and augmented reality over the next three years. This partnership aims to invest in the entrepreneurial spirit and integrate Metaverse tools and training into India's education system. Meta will also provide a curriculum on digital safety, online well-being, VR, and AR available on CBSE's website.

title: Unity Ads Now Offers Access to Meta Audience Network Through Unity Mediation
summary: Unity Ads has integrated Meta Audience Network into Unity Mediation, providing developers with streamlined self-serve access to a premium demand source. This partnership aims to maximize revenue for developers by offering competitive bidding and a comprehensive network of over 60 ad ecosystem partners. The integration is a significant step towards optimizing monetization and growth solutions within Unity Gaming Services.

title: Facebook exposes mercenary spy firms that targeted 50,000 people
summary: Meta Platforms Inc (FB.O) has exposed half a dozen mercenary spy firms for targeting approximately 50,000 people across its platforms through hacking and other abuses. This crackdown involved suspending 1,500 accounts and signals a broader push by tech companies and the U.S. government against digital espionage services. The firms, including Black Cube and BellTroX, were accused of various tactics from creating fake profiles to phishing attacks.

title: Focus: Boeing wants to build its next airplane in the 'metaverse'
summary: Boeing is launching an ambitious strategy to integrate a digital ecosystem for designing, producing, and servicing its aircraft, utilizing technologies like immersive 3-D engineering and HoloLens headsets. This "metaverse" approach aims to improve quality, safety, and efficiency, preventing issues like those encountered with the 737 MAX and 787 Dreamliner. While facing challenges and skepticism due to past technological hurdles and R&D cuts, Boeing believes this digital transformation is crucial for its future aircraft programs and competitive edge against rivals like Airbus.

title: Meta now listed as Facebook developer on Google Play and App Store
summary: Following Facebook's rebrand to Meta earlier this year, the company's Android and iOS apps, such as Messenger, now list "Meta Platforms, Inc." as the developer. This change applies primarily to apps directly associated with the Facebook name, while Instagram and WhatsApp still list their respective company names as developers. The update reflects the corporation's new identity but does not alter the user experience.

title: Investor Alert for Week Ended December 17, 2021
summary: This investor alert discusses the emerging metaverse, Web 3.0, and its potential to revolutionize various sectors including social interaction, commerce, and gaming, comparing its disruptive potential to the early internet. It covers investment opportunities in hardware, software, NFTs, and virtual real estate within this digital ecosystem. Additionally, the report provides an overview of performance and opportunities in airline, emerging markets, energy & natural resources, domestic equities, and crypto sectors, alongside a gold market update.

title: The Metaverse Is a $1 Trillion Revenue Opportunity. Here’s How to Invest
summary: The metaverse, a new iteration of the internet, is projected to be a trillion-dollar revenue opportunity, transforming how people work, play, socialize, and invest. This emerging digital ecosystem will feature virtual reality experiences, digital assets like NFTs, and virtual real estate, attracting interest from major tech companies, luxury brands, and investors. Early investment opportunities exist in hardware, software, and platforms operating within this evolving virtual world.

title: Decentraland Real Estate
summary: This report from Grayscale discusses the rising investment in the Web 3.0 metaverse sector, particularly focusing on Decentraland. It highlights the virtual real estate boom within Decentraland, driven by increasing user adoption and business activity, and examines the relationship between MANA token value and LAND prices. The report also projects significant growth opportunities for virtual worlds and Decentraland's position as a leading platform in this evolving digital economy.

title: Equinix acquires MainOne to enter African data center market
summary: Equinix, the world’s largest data center company, has acquired MainOne for $320 million, marking its entry into the African data center market. This strategic move aims to provide "continental edge" data center services in Africa, leveraging MainOne's extensive network infrastructure, including a 7k km submarine cable and over 1.2k km of terrestrial fiber. The acquisition is expected to close in Q1 2022 and will see MainOne's founder and over 500 employees join Equinix, enabling faster scaling and broader international customer reach.

title: GM is also dropping its CES exhibit, organizers still planning in-person show
summary: General Motors has announced it is moving to an all-digital approach for its CES 2022 activation, including CEO Mary Barra's keynote, due to the ongoing pandemic. GM joins a growing list of major companies, such as Google, Intel, and Amazon, that have pulled out of in-person participation, often citing concerns about the Omicron variant. Despite these withdrawals, CES organizers plan to proceed with the in-person event, implementing health measures like vaccination requirements and mask mandates.

title: Intel becomes the latest company to back away from an in-person CES
summary: Intel has announced it will minimize its in-person presence at CES 2022, opting for a digital-first approach due to growing concerns over the omicron variant. The company joins a growing list of major tech firms, including Lenovo, Waymo, T-Mobile, and Amazon, that are reducing or eliminating their physical attendance. Despite these numerous pullbacks, CES organizers maintain that the event will proceed with health protocols in place.

title: Boeing Wants to Build its Next Airplane in the 'Metaverse'
summary: Boeing plans to revolutionize its aircraft manufacturing by uniting design, production, and services under a single digital system, aiming to build its next airplane in the "metaverse" within the next two years. This digital transformation, involving 3-D designs, robots, and mixed reality headsets, seeks to improve quality, safety, and efficiency while reducing design-related issues. The initiative also comes as the company tries to regain trust after the 737 MAX crisis and avoid future manufacturing problems like those encountered with the 787 Dreamliner.

title: Israeli companies face Trojan horse dilemma
summary: Israeli cyberattack companies like Cognyte and Quadream are grappling with strategic decisions following the controversy surrounding NSO Group and its Pegasus spyware. These companies are weighing whether to fill the potential void left by NSO, scale back or sell off their own "Trojan horse" activities due to increasing scrutiny and diplomatic pressure, particularly from the US. The article highlights Cognyte's deliberations regarding its Trojan horse product and its declining share price, while also noting Quadream's similar considerations amidst opportunities to capture NSO's former clientele.

title: P&G cancels live appearances at CES tech show amid COVID-19 concerns
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced it is canceling its live appearances at the upcoming CES tech show in Las Vegas due to rising concerns over the coronavirus' omicron variant. Instead of a physical presence, P&G will host an all-virtual event on its pglifelab.com website, prioritizing the health and well-being of its employees and partners. This decision follows similar moves by other major companies like Amazon and Meta, despite CES's plans to continue the in-person event from January 5-8.

title: Facebook pushes ahead with Farley project in bet on offices
summary: Meta Platforms Inc., formerly Facebook, is moving forward with its expansion into the Farley Building in New York City, demonstrating a continued commitment to office spaces despite the pandemic's impact. The company plans to occupy 730,000 square feet, relocating employees there in early 2022, and outfits the space with extensive amenities. This expansion is a significant bet on the New York office market, particularly within a burgeoning technology and finance corridor near Madison Square Garden.

title: Social Media Company Quora Is Going Public: Here Are the Details
summary: Quora is considering going public, potentially following other social media companies like Reddit, Rumble, and TMTG. While no IPO date has been set, Reuters reported Quora could go public in 2022 with a valuation of $4 billion, a significant increase from its 2019 private funding. The company generates revenue through advertising and subscription products, aiming to become free-cash-flow-positive on ad revenue alone.

title: Devin Nunes officially resigns from Congress, clearing way to helm Trump's social media company
summary: Devin Nunes officially resigned from Congress to become CEO of former President Trump's media and technology company, Truth Social. Nunes, a staunch ally of Trump, will lead the new platform which aims to be an alternative to mainstream social media. His move signifies his continued loyalty to Trump and his transition from a congressional career focused initially on local issues to national security and defense of the former president.

title: Qualcomm, Microsoft partner on metaverse chip for AR glasses
summary: Qualcomm and Microsoft are collaborating on custom chips for lightweight augmented reality (AR) glasses, targeting both consumers and businesses for metaverse applications. The partnership aims to integrate these chips with Microsoft's Mesh software for virtual presence and Qualcomm's Snapdragon Spaces for AR functions like spatial mapping and hand-tracking. Though no release date was provided, the initiative seeks to advance wearable AR devices for broader adoption.

title: What Crypto-related ETFs Could Hit the US Market in 2022?
summary: The article discusses the potential for various crypto-related ETFs, particularly metaverse products, to launch in the US market in 2022, while the approval of spot bitcoin and ether futures products remains uncertain. Industry experts express apprehension about the immediate investability of metaverse ETFs due to potential crossover in holdings and a lack of pure-play names. There's also skepticism regarding the SEC's approval of a spot bitcoin ETF in 2022, with some analysts expecting an ether futures-based ETF to gain approval sooner.

title: P&G takes first step into the metaverse with BeautySphere
summary: P&G Beauty has entered the metaverse with the launch of BeautySphere, a virtual storytelling world accessible via desktop, which debuted at CES. This platform enables consumers to interact with P&G's brands through live content, panel discussions, and gamified challenges, focusing on the company's "Responsible Beauty" initiatives. BeautySphere aims to engage digitally-savvy consumers on a nascent virtual landscape, bridging virtual experiences with real-world impact, such as planting trees for reforestation efforts.

title: Trump’s social media app to launch in February, App Store listing says
summary: Donald Trump's new social media app, Truth Social, is set to launch on February 21, 2022, according to an Apple App Store listing. The launch comes 13 months after Trump was banned from major social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter. The app will offer features similar to Twitter and is the first of three planned stages for the Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), which also plans a subscription video service and a podcast network.

title: Meta leases up all office space in Austin's tallest tower in historic deal
summary: Meta Platforms Inc., the parent company of Facebook, has leased all 589,000 square feet of office space at Sixth and Guadalupe, which will be Austin's tallest building. This historic deal ends months of speculation and signifies Meta's commitment to expand its presence in Austin, with plans to hire hundreds more employees in the city. The company will also maintain its existing downtown Austin offices.

title: Tech Moves: Adaptive CFO to resign; Meta comms exec departs; AI vet joins Absci board; new Zymeworks CEO
summary: This article details several significant personnel changes in the tech and biotech sectors, including Chad Cohen's resignation as CFO of Adaptive Biotechnologies, Joseph Sirosh's appointment to the Absci board, John Pinette's departure from Meta, and Kenneth Galbraith becoming the new CEO of Zymeworks. It highlights the impact of these moves on the respective companies and their financial performance or strategic direction.

title: Meta Platforms adds DoorDash CEO Tony Xu to board of directors
summary: Meta Platforms has announced that DoorDash CEO Tony Xu has been appointed to its board of directors. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg praised Xu for building a successful service for millions of people and numerous businesses. Xu co-founded DoorDash in 2013 at Stanford University.

title: Exercise by Accident: VR Games To Help You Work Out at Home
summary: This article highlights how virtual reality (VR) games can offer a fun and effective way to exercise at home, even for those who find traditional workouts challenging. It categorizes various VR games into dedicated fitness apps, rhythm-based games, action titles, sporty simulations, and training programs, detailing how each can contribute to physical activity and fitness goals. The piece also mentions Oculus Move, a system-level fitness tracker, to monitor calorie burn across VR apps and encourages readers to share their favorite VR exercise routines.

title: Facebook faces $3.2 bln UK class action over market dominance
summary: Facebook, now Meta Platforms, is facing a £2.3 billion ($3.2 billion) class-action lawsuit in the UK for allegedly abusing its market dominance by exploiting the personal data of 44 million users between 2015 and 2019. The lawsuit, brought by Liza Lovdahl Gormsen, claims Facebook imposed unfair terms requiring users to surrender valuable personal data to access its network. This legal challenge comes shortly after Facebook lost an attempt to strike out an antitrust lawsuit from the Federal Trade Commission in the U.S.

title: Facebook loses bid to dismiss users’ data-privacy antitrust claims
summary: A California federal judge has partially denied Facebook's motion to dismiss antitrust claims from consumers and advertisers, allowing complaints regarding false data privacy representations and an agreement with Google to proceed. While certain claims against Meta Platforms Inc. were dismissed, plaintiffs have been granted 45 days to refile amended complaints. This decision follows another recent ruling against Facebook in an antitrust case filed by the Federal Trade Commission.

title: A Guide to Investing in Emerging Asian Markets Outside of China
summary: This article discusses investment opportunities in five emerging Asian markets—Pakistan, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Vietnam, and the Philippines—dubbed "Asian Growth Cubs" by Dawn Global Management. These countries offer significant growth potential for investors looking for exposure to Asian markets outside of China and India, with a collective GDP similar to India's but a much lower market cap. The article highlights the Asian Growth Cubs ETF (CUBS) as a way for foreign investors to access these markets, focusing on industries like healthcare, telecom, and technology.

title: Certification programs build digital skills
summary: The Economic Development Corporation Michigan City (EDCMC) and Goodwill Industries of Michiana are collaborating to offer certification programs for digital skill enhancement. These online courses, including Facebook Social Media Marketing and Google IT Support, aim to help community members earn stackable certificates in high-demand fields. The programs are designed to assist individuals in overcoming barriers to education and employment by providing coursework, mentorship, and job placement services.

title: Mother sues Meta and Snap over tween daughter’s suicide
summary: An American mother has filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms Inc. and Snap Inc., alleging their social media platforms, Instagram and Snapchat, are responsible for her 11-year-old daughter's suicide. The lawsuit claims the daughter developed an "extreme addiction" to these platforms, which the companies allegedly knew were harmful to minor users. This legal action comes amid increasing scrutiny and ongoing investigations into the mental health impact of social media on young people.

title: Microsoft secures IPs like Call of Duty and Candy Crash to boost its metaverse ambitions, analyst says
summary: Microsoft's $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard is seen as a strategic move to bolster its metaverse ambitions, according to analyst Joost Rietveld. The deal secures popular gaming franchises like Call of Duty and Candy Crush, potentially differentiating Microsoft's Game Pass service and influencing cross-platform availability. While Microsoft has committed to honoring existing agreements, allowing Call of Duty to remain on PlayStation for now, the long-term impact on platform exclusivity for other IPs remains uncertain.

title: What a Bristol-Myers project to monitor off-label prescribing says about future uses of A.I.
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb collaborated with Cortical.io to utilize AI for monitoring off-label drug prescribing by analyzing social media data. The pilot project successfully identified off-label uses of drugs, including an unexpected finding for Suboxone, demonstrating the potential of natural language processing and less data-intensive AI methods for post-market surveillance. This initiative highlights the growing importance of AI in patient safety and the value of brain-inspired AI research.

title: The 3 Best Carbon Stocks of 2022
summary: This article highlights the top three carbon-related investment opportunities for 2022, emphasizing the growing importance of carbon markets and green investing. It details the KraneShares Global Carbon Strategy ETF (KRBN) for broad market exposure, Carbon Streaming Corporation (NETZ/OFSTF) as an early mover in carbon credit streaming, and Brookfield Renewable Partners (BEP) for a more conservative renewable energy play. The article underscores how increasing net-zero ambitions among corporations and rising awareness of climate change will drive investor interest in these sectors.

title: Timing Is Everything For ETFs
summary: Thematic ETFs, which invest in specific market themes, have grown significantly. Their success often depends heavily on the timing of their launch, sometimes due to unintentional events, as exemplified by the ETFMG Prime Cyber Security ETF (HACK) benefiting from major cybersecurity breaches shortly after its inception. Conversely, funds like the Sprott Buzz Social Media Insights ETF (BUZ) failed due to poor timing, while later similar entrants thrived by tapping into peak market interest.

title: Morgan Stanley Sees $8 Trillion Metaverse Market — In China Alone
summary: Morgan Stanley predicts an $8 trillion metaverse market in China alone, replacing the mobile internet with a more "immersive experience." The investment bank acknowledges significant technological and regulatory hurdles for mass adoption, estimating an initial total addressable market of $4 trillion before expanding to $8 trillion as it disrupts offline activities.

title: Beer Summit Takeaways: A-B CEO Previews Bud Light Next; Digital Marketing Opportunities on Facebook, Instagram; Lots of Seltzer Talk
summary: The article summarizes key discussions from Beer Business Daily’s Beer Industry Summit, detailing Anheuser-Busch InBev's CEO Brendan Whitworth's insights on Bud Light Next and e-commerce, Meta's Pablo Merheb's presentation on digital marketing for alcohol brands, and growth updates from Diageo’s Lone River Ranch Water, Molson Coors' Topo Chico Hard Seltzer, and Gopuff's expansion into beverage alcohol delivery. Constellation Brands CEO Bill Newlands also provided updates on the company’s Mexican import portfolio and Fresca Mixed.

title: Amazon and Microsoft led the world in corporate purchases of clean energy in 2021
summary: Amazon and Microsoft were global leaders in corporate clean energy power purchase agreements in 2021, with Amazon holding the top spot for the second consecutive year. Combined, the two tech giants procured 12.4 GW of wind and solar power, contributing significantly to a record-setting year for corporate carbon-free energy deals. Both companies are committed to achieving 100% renewable energy for their operations by 2025, with Microsoft aiming for 24/7 clean energy by 2030.

title: Meta Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Results
summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. reported solid financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2021, driven by continued growth in user engagement and business use of its services. The company highlighted significant investments in key growth areas such as Reels, commerce, and virtual reality, alongside a new financial reporting structure separating its Family of Apps (FoA) and Reality Labs (RL) segments. Meta also announced its upcoming ticker symbol change to 'META' and provided an outlook for Q1 2022 revenue, anticipating headwinds from increased competition, platform changes, and macroeconomic factors.

title: TMUS Stock: 9 Reasons Why T-Mobile Investors Are Dialing Up Gains Today
summary: T-Mobile US (TMUS) stock is experiencing a significant surge after the telecommunications company released its fourth-quarter 2021 earnings report. Despite a slight revenue miss, diluted earnings per share surpassed Wall Street expectations, and a strong 2022 outlook, including projections for 5 million to 5.5 million postpaid net customer additions and significant merger synergies, contributed to investor optimism. The positive report has led to heavy trading activity, with TMUS stock up over 10% as of Thursday afternoon.

title: Document
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2021, showing increased net sales but decreased operating cash flow due to higher costs. The company reported a significant net income increase in Q4 2021, boosted by a valuation gain from its investment in Rivian Automotive. Amazon also highlighted continued investments in Prime benefits, expansion of AWS services, and initiatives in environmental protection and community support.

title: Amazon raises Prime membership fees to offset growing costs
summary: Amazon announced it is increasing its Prime membership fees in the United States to offset rising shipping costs and wages, despite exceeding profit expectations for the holiday quarter. The annual membership fee will go up to $139 from $119, effective February 18 for new members. The company's shares saw a significant rise following the announcement, although it also forecast first-quarter sales below Wall Street estimates.

title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway Is Now Bigger Than Meta
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has surpassed Meta Platforms in market capitalization, marking a significant shift in stock-market standing. This article highlights Berkshire Hathaway's increasing valuation relative to Meta.

title: H&R Block rolls out mobile banking in time for tax season
summary: H&R Block has launched a new mobile banking service called Spruce, in partnership with Meta Financial’s MetaBank, to attract and serve clients, particularly those without traditional bank accounts. The service offers a spending account, debit card, mobile app, and savings features to help customers manage their finances and budget for specific goals. Spruce aims to address the financial health of many Americans, especially during tax season, by providing a low-to-no-fee banking product that facilitates direct deposit of tax refunds and offers features like early paycheck access and fee-free overdraft protection.

title: Metaverse stocks Nvidia and Roblox fall as Facebook parent Meta's Web3 business reports massive loss
summary: Shares of metaverse-related companies like Roblox, Nvidia, and Matterport fell after Meta Platforms reported a significant operating loss of $10 billion in its Web3 division, Reality Labs, for 2021. The news led to a market value wipeout of over $200 billion for Meta and a sell-off across various tech stocks connected to the metaverse concept. This downturn highlights concerns following Meta's aggressive push into the metaverse space.

title: Zuckerberg loses $29b in a day as Meta shares crash
summary: Mark Zuckerberg's net worth plummeted by $29 billion in a single day after Meta Platforms Inc.'s stock experienced a record dive following a disappointing earnings forecast. Meta's shares fell 26%, wiping out over $200 billion in market value, the largest single-day loss for a US company. This decline pushed Zuckerberg to the twelfth spot on Forbes' real-time billionaires list, with analysts citing Apple's privacy changes and increased competition from rivals like TikTok and YouTube as contributing factors.

title: Amazon set for historic market cap gain after Meta’s epic loss
summary: Amazon is projected to add approximately $155 billion in market value if its stock's 11% pre-market gain holds, placing it among the top five single-day gains in U.S. stock market history. This surge follows strong performance in its cloud computing division and a price increase for Amazon Prime, counteracting fears sparked by Meta Platforms Inc.'s recent significant market cap loss. Amazon's expected gain comes after it experienced its own decline, losing $119 billion in market value the day prior due to Meta's earnings flop.

title: Amazon share price surges 19% in post-market trading as company announces price hike in Prime membership
summary: Amazon's stock surged 19% in post-market trading after the e-commerce giant reported better-than-expected profits and announced an increase in its Prime membership price. This rise, along with strong earnings from Snap and Pinterest, helped to alleviate concerns following Meta Platforms' significant stock crash. Despite the after-hours rebound, Amazon and Snap shares only returned to mid-January levels, highlighting the extent of a recent selloff.

title: Meta Extended Its Buybacks Into January—Just Before the Stock Slid
summary: Meta Platforms aggressively repurchased its stock in the fourth quarter of 2021 and continued these buybacks into January 2022. This occurred just prior to the release of the company's disappointing fourth-quarter earnings report. The earnings report subsequently caused a significant decline in Meta's stock price.

title: Meta Stock Drop Biggest in History – Apple App Tracking Transparency a Factor
summary: Meta's stock plunged by 26% on Thursday, resulting in a US$251.3 billion loss in market value, making it the largest single-day stock drop in history. This significant decline was largely attributed to Apple's App Tracking Transparency (ATT) privacy policy changes, which have impacted Meta's advertising revenue. Mark Zuckerberg also acknowledged increased competition from platforms like TikTok and a shift towards short-form video as contributing factors.

title: TelevisaUnivision Hires Multimedia Ad Sales Execs | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
summary: TelevisaUnivision has announced the hiring of two new senior multimedia ad sales executives, Rob McGovern and Richard Bertodatti, to bolster its sales efforts. McGovern will lead West Coast national sales, while Bertodatti will manage business with major media agencies and the Boston territory. Both will report to John Kozack, Executive VP of multimedia sales, with a focus on showcasing the company's unique opportunities to marketers and leveraging the power of Hispanic audiences.

title: Meta rivalry with Apple inflamed as Facebook parent company share price plummets
summary: Meta's stock price plummeted by 26%, wiping out approximately $220bn in market value, primarily due to "headwinds" caused by Apple's new iOS privacy changes. Mark Zuckerberg blamed these changes, which restrict advertisers' ability to target ads, estimating a $10bn impact on Meta's business. In contrast, other tech companies like Snap, Amazon, and Pinterest reported strong ad revenue or stock growth, indicating that Apple's privacy updates did not affect all companies equally.

title: Traditional conglomerates such as GE, J&J and Toshiba are moving in a new direction
summary: Traditional conglomerates like General Electric, Johnson & Johnson, and Toshiba are breaking up their companies to increase shareholder value and simplify management. This trend is driven by past financial difficulties and the complexities of their diversified operations. In contrast, modern tech giants like Amazon and Meta thrive as conglomerates by leveraging platform-based models and network effects, which offer a different approach to managing varied businesses.

title: Opinion: $1.4 trillion? Big Tech’s pandemic year produces mind-boggling financial results
summary: In 2021, despite supply-chain disruptions, labor shortages, and rising prices, major tech companies including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft achieved staggering financial results. They collectively saw over $320 billion in profit on $1.4 trillion in sales, with profits increasing more than 55% and sales growing 27% from an already record-setting base. This performance highlights Big Tech's resilience and expanding economic influence, making their combined sales comparable to a top-15 global economy.

title: Amazon hiking base salary cap to $350,000 for corporate, tech workers
summary: Amazon has announced a significant increase in its base salary cap for corporate and tech workers, raising it from $160,000 to $350,000. This move aims to enhance the company's competitiveness in a challenging labor market and attract and retain top talent. The company indicated that these increases are "much more considerable" than in previous years, aligning its pay structure more closely with other major tech firms.

title: Peter Thiel to leave Meta board to pursue Trump political agenda
summary: Peter Thiel, a long-serving board member of Meta Platforms Inc. and early investor in Facebook, is stepping down from the company's board after its annual shareholder meeting in May. Thiel intends to focus on increasing his political support for former President Donald Trump's agenda during the 2022 election, aiming to avoid being a "distraction" for Meta. He plans to back Republican candidates like Blake Masters and JD Vance who align with Trump's political aims.

title: The metaverse is ‘particularly hard to predict,’ says Unity’s AR/VR chief
summary: Timoni West, Unity's AR/VR chief, believes that while the excitement around spatial computing and the metaverse is justified, the exact future applications are "particularly hard to predict." She draws parallels to the early days of the internet, where people correctly envisioned themes like online shopping but failed to foresee the ultimate form it would take. West suggests that current attempts to apply existing patterns to new technologies, such as realistic avatars in virtual spaces, will likely evolve into something completely different over time.

title: Peter Thiel to step down from board of Facebook parent Meta
summary: Tech billionaire Peter Thiel is stepping down from the board of Meta Platforms Inc., the parent company of Facebook. Thiel, who co-founded PayPal and was an early investor in Facebook, has served on the board since 2015 and will not seek re-election at the company's annual stockholders meeting in May.

title: Aussie funds exposed to the Meta rout: Charts of the Week
summary: Australian managed funds and popular index-tracking ETFs, including those from Magellan, Hyperion, and Lakehouse, were significantly impacted by Meta Platforms' sharp 26% stock drop, the largest one-day market capitalization loss in US history. This "Meta rout" contributed to new year woes for growth investors, although some losses were mitigated by strong performance from Amazon.com positions within several of these funds. Sustainable funds generally avoided the Meta selloff due to ESG-related exclusions stemming from privacy concerns.

title: Meta Is Now Calling Out Google Over Apple's App Privacy Rules
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. is publicly criticizing Google, alleging it has an unfair advantage under Apple's new privacy policies. While Meta's apps must ask users for tracking consent, Google's search and browser functions do not, leading to a shift in advertiser budgets towards Google. This comes after Meta's revenue took a multibillion-dollar hit due to its inability to gather as much data on iPhone users.

title: Better Buy: Meta Platforms vs. PayPal Holdings
summary: This article compares Meta Platforms and PayPal Holdings after both companies experienced significant stock price drops due to disappointing earnings reports and future guidance. It outlines the reasons behind their respective crashes, including Apple's privacy changes and TikTok competition for Meta, and supply chain issues and increased competition for PayPal. The author ultimately argues that Meta is a more compelling investment due to its diversification, lower valuation, and wider moat, despite current risks for both stocks.

title: Gartner: A quarter of consumers will use the metaverse daily by 2026
summary: A Gartner report predicts that by 2026, 25% of consumers will spend at least one hour daily in the metaverse for various activities like work, shopping, or entertainment. The report advises organizations against over-investing in single metaverse components due to its early and disconnected stage of adoption but emphasizes the potential for digital currencies and immersive online events. Retailers are already engaging with the metaverse by partnering with platforms like Roblox and filing trademarks for virtual goods, while tech giants like Meta and Microsoft are investing heavily in its development.

title: YouTube floats ideas of verifying NFTs, watching games in metaverse
summary: YouTube is exploring using blockchain technology and NFTs to help creators find new ways to monetize content by offering verifiable digital assets. The company also suggested ideas for the metaverse, focusing on enhancing social viewing experiences, particularly for gaming content, to allow users to watch videos together in a virtual environment. These initiatives aim to cut down on fraud in the digital art market and improve user engagement.

title: Qualcomm Expands XR & Metaverse Investment With The Formation of XR Labs Europe
summary: Qualcomm Technologies has opened new Extended Reality (XR) Labs across six European cities to expand its investment in XR and the metaverse. These labs will focus on XR R&D, engineering, and key technology areas like hand tracking, 3D mapping, and multi-user experiences to make XR accessible and foster the Snapdragon Spaces XR Developer Platform. The initiative aims to support the development of lightweight head-worn devices and innovative experiences across various sectors, leveraging Europe's strong AR/VR community and Qualcomm's leadership in mobile and XR technology.

title: Expedia CEO says the metaverse doesn’t pose a threat to what he calls ‘real-verse’ travel
summary: Expedia CEO Peter Kern believes the metaverse does not pose a competitive threat to real-world travel, which he calls the "real-verse." While acknowledging the intrigue, Kern stated that virtual experiences cannot replicate the life-changing nature of physical travel to places like Paris or national parks. He expressed confidence that people will continue to prioritize real-world experiences, despite the growth in virtual reality investments.

title: TikTok Inks Major Lease in Austin
summary: TikTok has signed a major sublease for over 125,000 square feet at 300 Colorado, a 32-story high-rise in downtown Austin. The social media company will occupy the top six floors of the building, which was completed in 2021. This move comes as the Austin office market experienced significant activity, including a large lease by Meta Platforms, despite overall office vacancy remaining above the city's average.

title: Stanley Druckenmiller Buys Chevron as Family Offices Reveal Stock Picks
summary: Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office sold its Meta Platforms Inc. position and bought Chevron, indicating a shift away from big tech. Similarly, George Soros's family office reduced its stakes in Amazon.com, Alphabet, and a Nasdaq 100 ETF. These moves suggest a trend among some wealthy investors to re-evaluate their portfolios regarding large technology companies.

title: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sues Facebook alleging social media giant violated state law
summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has filed a lawsuit against Facebook's parent company, Meta Platforms, Inc., alleging that the social media giant violated state law by collecting and storing users' biometric information (facial features) from photos and videos without proper consent. The lawsuit claims Facebook shared this data and failed to destroy it in a timely manner, exposing millions of Texans to risks. Facebook has denied the claims, stating they are "without merit."

title: Texas sues Facebook parent company over use of facial recognition technology
summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms Inc., the parent company of Facebook, alleging violations of state privacy and anti-deceptive trade practice laws due to its past use of facial recognition technology. The suit claims Facebook failed to disclose biometric data collection, transmitted information to third parties, and did not delete data within a reasonable timeframe, seeking billions in damages. Meta has stated the claims are without merit and plans to defend itself vigorously, while political rivals have criticized Paxton's timing and use of outside counsel.

title: Meta's Facebook to pay $90 million to settle privacy lawsuit over user tracking
summary: Meta Platforms Inc (Facebook) has agreed to pay $90 million to settle a long-standing privacy lawsuit. The lawsuit accused Facebook of tracking users' internet activity, including visits to outside websites with "like" buttons, even after they logged out, and then compiling these browsing histories for advertisers. The settlement still requires court approval and mandates the deletion of improperly collected data, addressing claims of violating federal and state privacy and wiretapping laws.

title: Facebook Stops Fighting Wiretap Act Litigation After More Than a Decade
summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. (formerly Facebook) has proposed a $90 million national class action settlement in its long-running Facebook Internet Tracking Litigation, involving over 124 million Americans. The lawsuit stemmed from allegations that Facebook tracked user activity on non-Facebook sites using "Like" buttons between April 2010 and September 2011, violating federal and California Wiretap Act laws. While the settlement brings closure to a decade-long legal battle and requires deletion of old data, it also highlights potential future legal scrutiny for third-party trackers.

title: Trump's new social media application 'Truth Social' begins gradual rollout
summary: Donald Trump's "Truth Social" app began a gradual rollout on Sunday, with the aim of being fully operational in the US by the end of March. The platform is intended as an alternative to major social media sites that banned Trump after the January 6, 2021 Capitol assault. Former congressman Devin Nunes, CEO of Trump Media & Technology Group, stated that the app would be available on the Apple App Store, celebrating the return of free speech for those who felt their voices were canceled.

title: How DBMS is Used by Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company
summary: This article examines how Database Management Systems (DBMS) are crucial for organizations to efficiently store, retrieve, and manage data. It provides case studies of how major companies like Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company leverage DBMS to address challenges, optimize operations, and maintain data integrity and security, highlighting the benefits over traditional file systems. The article demonstrates the real-world applications and positive outcomes of integrating DBMS in various industries.

title: 11 Inspiring Women Who Pivoted into Tech Careers After Completing 2U-Powered Boot Camps
summary: This article highlights 11 women who successfully transitioned into tech careers after completing 2U-powered boot camps in various disciplines like coding, data science, cybersecurity, and fintech. The featured individuals come from diverse backgrounds, including full-time moms, mid-career pivoters, and those affected by pandemic layoffs. Their stories showcase how these boot camps equipped them with the skills needed to land new roles at companies such as Meta, Infosys, Johnson & Johnson, Lowe's, Citibank, and others, acting as role models and transforming the tech landscape.

title: College could take place in the metaverse, but these problems must be overcome first
summary: Higher education in the US faces significant challenges including rising tuition, student debt, and dissatisfaction with online learning. The metaverse could offer a solution by creating more immersive remote learning experiences, but it also presents new ethical and practical problems. Five key issues to address include ensuring academic freedom on private platforms, maintaining student focus in a highly distracting virtual environment, improving nonverbal communication through avatars, fostering a sense of community outside of physical campuses, and preventing new digital divides.

title: Google, Meta face penalties in Russia as deadline passes to open local offices
summary: Google and Meta are among several internet companies facing potential penalties in Russia for failing to establish local offices and comply with a new communications law. Russia's state communications regulator, Roskomnadzor, had set a deadline of the end of February for these companies to open local offices or face restrictions. The move is part of Russia's broader effort to control internet content, with fines previously issued for failing to censor anti-government content, and recent curtailments of access to platforms like Facebook in retaliation for censoring state media.

title: Qualcomm Extends Connectivity Leadership with World's First and Fastest Wi-Fi 7 Commercial Solution
summary: Qualcomm Technologies has introduced FastConnect 7800, the industry's first Wi-Fi 7 commercial solution, featuring High Band Simultaneous (HBS) Multi-Link technology for superior speeds and ultra-low latency. This advanced connectivity system also incorporates next-generation Intelligent Dual Bluetooth, enhancing Snapdragon Sound and Bluetooth LE Audio with improved range, faster pairing, and seamless device switching. The FastConnect 7800 is designed to deliver unparalleled wireless performance and power efficiency for a wide range of client devices.

title: AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, TSMC and others join Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group
summary: Leading semiconductor companies including AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC have formed the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) industry consortium. This group aims to establish an open chiplet ecosystem by standardizing die-to-die interconnects, with the UCIe 1.0 specification already ratified. This initiative leverages existing PCI Express and Compute Express Link standards to enable easier mixing and matching of chiplet components from multiple vendors for System-on-Chip (SoC) construction.

title: Apple, Netflix, TikTok strike back against Russian state media content
summary: Several major tech and entertainment companies, including Apple, Netflix, and TikTok, are taking action against Russian state media and suspending services in Russia following the invasion of Ukraine. This includes Netflix refusing to carry Russian federal channels, Apple pausing product sales and limiting services, and social media platforms restricting access to and demoting content from outlets like RT and Sputnik due to concerns about propaganda and disinformation. The moves reflect a global condemnation of Russia's actions and a united front from U.S. businesses.

title: Leaders in Semiconductors, Packaging, IP Suppliers, Foundries, and Cloud Service Providers Join Forces to Standardize Chiplet Ecosystem
summary: A consortium of leading technology companies, including ASE, AMD, Arm, Google Cloud, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC, has formed to standardize the chiplet ecosystem. They have ratified the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) 1.0 specification, an open industry standard for die-to-die interconnects, aiming to enable multi-vendor compatibility for System-on-Chip construction. The consortium is open for membership and plans to develop future generations of the UCIe technology.

title: Tripadvisor, Google Maps Suspend Reviews of Some Russian Listings
summary: Google Maps and Tripadvisor have temporarily suspended new user reviews for certain listings in Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus. This action was taken in response to a flood of political statements posted as reviews, driven by a social media campaign urging activists to communicate with Russians via these platforms about the war in Ukraine. The companies aim to prevent the publishing of off-topic and abusive content.

title: Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group combines AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, TSMC and more
summary: The Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group, formed by major tech companies like AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, and TSMC, has established a new industry consortium. Their goal is to standardize die-to-die interconnect guidelines and foster an open chiplet ecosystem, developing the UCIe 1.0 specification for interoperable multi-vendor chiplet components. This initiative aims to drive innovation in customizable package-level integration and address future challenges in semiconductor systems.

title: Spotify closes its office in Russia in response to attack on Ukraine
summary: Spotify announced the indefinite closure of its office in Russia in response to the country's attack on Ukraine. The music streaming platform stated its priority is its employees' safety and ensuring access to information. Spotify has also restricted the discoverability of Russian state-affiliated media and removed content from RT and Sputnik in several markets, while matching employee donations for humanitarian aid.

title: Goldman Sachs-Backed Virtual Beauty App Developer To Go Public In $1 Billion SPAC Deal
summary: Perfect Corp., a Taiwan-headquartered virtual beauty try-on app developer backed by Goldman Sachs, announced its plan to go public in the U.S. through a SPAC merger valued at $1 billion. The combination with Nasdaq-listed Provident Acquisition Corp. is expected to raise up to $335 million, including a $50 million PIPE investment from investors like Chanel and Shiseido. CEO Alice Chang stated the company aims to expand into Southeast Asia and the Middle East, and further integrate its augmented reality technologies across more platforms and categories, including the metaverse.

title: How Hyperscale Data Centers are reshaping India’s IT
summary: Hyperscale data centers are critical infrastructure for companies like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, providing dedicated computing resources to handle massive user demands. These facilities are essential for the digital economy, supporting everything from emails to online shopping, and their importance has grown with trends like remote work and emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. India is poised for significant growth in its data center industry, driven by government incentives and an increasing need for robust data storage and processing capabilities, despite environmental concerns related to energy consumption.

title: The cloud over commercial real estate lingers
summary: The commercial real estate market, particularly office spaces, continues to face challenges despite an initial return to optimism after the pandemic's early days. While some global forecasts are cautiously positive, the underlying issues of vacancy rates, decreasing property values, and the shift to remote work persist, leading to conversions of office spaces into residential units and increased incentives from landlords. The long-term impact on property valuations and investment returns remains a significant concern for the industry.

title: Industry Leaders Join Forces to Standardize Chiplet Ecosystem
summary: A consortium of industry leaders, including AMD, Arm, Google Cloud, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, TSMC, and ASE, has formed to standardize die-to-die interconnects and foster an open chiplet ecosystem. They have ratified the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) 1.0 specification, an open industry standard for package-level connectivity. This initiative aims to reduce development time and cost, promoting customizable and interoperable chiplet designs for future silicon innovations.

title: This CEO Has Purchased Over $1 Billion Worth Of His Own Stock Over The Last Year
summary: Dustin Moskovitz, co-founder of Meta Platforms and Asana Inc., has made an aggressive insider stock purchase, buying over $1 billion worth of Asana shares since June 2021. He now owns more than 16.5 million shares, representing about 21% of the company. This comes as Asana, a SaaS company, experienced strong demand during the pandemic but has seen its stock price tumble recently.

title: Blue Cross Blue Shield Owner Anthem Seeks to Rebrand to Elevance Health
summary: Anthem Inc., owner of several Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, plans to rebrand as Elevance Health Inc. to reflect a broader business focus beyond traditional health insurance. The company has diversified into areas like behavioral health, home-based care, and data analytics, seeking to achieve a premium valuation similar to UnitedHealth Group. While the new name aims to resonate with Wall Street and employees, branding experts suggest it might be difficult to connect with consumers who will still encounter the Anthem brand through their health coverage.

title: Biden must safeguard Russian internet access, civil society warns
summary: Civil society groups are urging the Biden administration to protect internet providers in Russia from sanctions, arguing that cutting off web access would isolate dissidents and strengthen the Kremlin's control. They recommend that the Office of Foreign Asset Controls formally authorize U.S. internet services, software, and hardware to preserve web access, citing precedents from past sanctions campaigns. The groups warn that without clear guidance, individuals in Russia could be cut off from vital internet services.

title: Russia says it will block Instagram
summary: Russia announced it would block Instagram, blaming a recent change in Meta's hate-speech policy that temporarily allowed some users to call for violence against Russians in the context of the Ukraine war. This move is part of Russia's broader effort to control information flow and prevent its citizens from accessing uncensored news about the invasion. The ban is expected to affect 80 million Russian users.

title: ‘The Dirty Dozen List’ – Corporations Enable and Profit from Sexual Exploitation
summary: The National Center on Sexual Exploitation (NCOSE) has released its annual "Dirty Dozen List," highlighting twelve mainstream entities accused of facilitating and profiting from sexual abuse and exploitation. The list includes technology giants like Google, Meta, Discord, and others, pointing to various ways they enable access to harmful content or profit from commercial sex industries. NCOSE details specific examples for each company and offers ways for the public to take action against these practices.

title: Metaverse Technology Redefining Digital Experience
summary: The metaverse is emerging as a significant technological advancement, moving beyond gaming to redefine digital experiences across various industries. Companies like Facebook (Meta), Nike, and Microsoft are investing heavily, with projections indicating global metaverse revenue could approach $800 billion by 2024. While offering potential for retail, enterprise solutions, and new markets like virtual real estate and entertainment, the metaverse also faces challenges related to data security, legal frameworks, skilled resources, VR device limitations, and potential negative societal impacts.

title: Russia to block Instagram over ‘death to invaders’ posting rule
summary: Russia plans to block Instagram and has launched a criminal case against its owner, Meta Platforms Inc., following Meta's decision to allow posts calling for violence against Russian forces. This move comes as an escalation in Russia's confrontation with US-based social media platforms, with Moscow alleging that Instagram is spreading calls for violence against Russian citizens and military personnel. Meta has defended its decision as a temporary measure in extraordinary circumstances, aimed at protecting Ukrainians' freedom of speech in self-defense.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO Says Ostracizing Russia Isn’t the Finance Industry’s Job
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon stated that it is not the finance industry's job to ostracize Russia, but rather to follow government sanctions. He emphasized that businesses should implement policies set by the government, agreeing with the sanctions against Russia's actions in Ukraine. Despite this stance, the article highlights Goldman Sachs's historical involvement in Russia's economic policy and its mixed record on activism.

title: Aptos raises $200M to bring the Diem blockchain back to life
summary: Aptos Labs, a startup founded by former employees of Meta's Diem blockchain project, has raised $200 million in strategic funding led by Andreessen Horowitz. The company aims to develop a safe and scalable blockchain network, learning from Diem's regulatory challenges. Aptos is building its own open-source blockchain for Web3 applications and expects to launch its public mainnet in the third quarter of 2022.

title: ProShares Launches Metaverse ETF, Expands Innovative Fund Lineup to the Internet’s Next Frontier
summary: ProShares has launched a new Metaverse ETF (VERS) designed to offer investors access to companies at the forefront of the metaverse's發展. The ETF tracks the Solactive Metaverse Theme Index, which includes 40 companies across various industries, from device makers to social media platforms. This initiative builds on ProShares' history of product innovation, including the first bitcoin-linked ETF, and aims to capitalize on the metaverse's potential to revolutionize industries.

title: Why banks and NATO are worrying about a future ‘Quantum attack’
summary: The article discusses the growing concern among banks and organizations like NATO about the potential for "quantum attacks" as quantum computing technology advances. Andersen Cheng, CEO of Post Quantum, warns that powerful quantum computers capable of cracking current encryption methods may be closer than initially thought, posing a significant threat to critical communications, financial data, and cryptocurrencies. The piece highlights how various nations are investing heavily in quantum technology and the commercial sector is beginning to prepare for this shift.

title: The Impact of Design on the Employee Experience
summary: Workday's Chief Design Officer, Jeff Gelfuso, emphasizes the importance of delivering seamless and engaging end-to-end experiences for employees within enterprise software, mirroring consumer software expectations. He discusses how Workday is achieving this through simplification, personalization, connectedness, and data-driven insights. The article highlights key design principles and Workday's initiatives like Engage, Everywhere, and Empower to improve the employee experience.

title: Facebook Continues To Lose Out On User Time; Netherlands Data Center Plans Face Opposition
summary: Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: FB) is experiencing a decline in user engagement on Facebook, as reported by BuzzFeed CEO Jonah Peretti, which negatively impacts its commerce revenues. Concurrently, Meta's plans for a large data center in Zeewolde, Netherlands, are facing significant political opposition after the Leefbaar Zeewolde party, which campaigned against the project, won a majority in the local elections. This comes at a time when Meta is also dealing with internal pressure from employees affected by plunging stock prices.

title: Towards The Distant Virtual World: Vitalii Vashchuk Shares Insights
summary: Vitalii Vashchuk, Director and Gaming Technologist at EPAM Systems, shared his insights on the metaverse's evolution and the underlying technologies. He describes the metaverse as a concept aimed at enhancing communication and experiences, offering greater freedom than Web2.0. Key technologies enabling the metaverse include Blockchain, NFTs, AI, and IoT.

title: Brookfield agrees to buy Hibernia REIT for $1.2 billion
summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. has reached an agreement to acquire Hibernia REIT Plc for approximately 1.09 billion euros ($1.2 billion) in cash, causing Hibernia's shares to surge to a record high. The deal, which offers a 33.9% premium over Hibernia's average share price, sees Brookfield expanding its real estate portfolio in Dublin, a market where tech giants are rapidly growing. Brookfield is actively investing in European office landlords, capitalizing on market uncertainty and discounts to asset values.

title: Amazon Stock Rally Erases Losses for the Year
summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares rallied, becoming the first megacap tech stock to recover its losses for the year,

title: Vietnam says over 3,200 "toxic" social media posts removed in Q1
summary: Vietnam's information ministry announced that social media platforms removed over 3,200 "toxic" posts and videos in the first quarter of the year at the government's request. This action is part of Vietnam's ongoing efforts to control online content, with companies like Facebook, YouTube, and TikTok complying with requests to take down content deemed false, offensive, or anti-state. The ruling Communist Party maintains strict media censorship, and new internet laws have raised concerns about potential crackdowns on dissent.

title: Meta to open new engineering hub in Toronto, expects to create 2,500 jobs
summary: Meta Platforms Inc. is establishing a new engineering hub in Toronto, aiming to create up to 2,500 high-tech jobs focused on immersive online experiences and the metaverse. These roles will offer both in-office and remote work options, making them accessible to Canadians nationwide. Additionally, Meta will invest $510,000 in grants for Canadian research labs to foster metaverse-related innovations.

title: Silicon Ranch, TVA, Meta break ground on 70MW solar facility in Tennessee
summary: Silicon Ranch, the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), and Meta have commenced construction on the new 70MW McKellar Solar Farm in Madison County, Tennessee. This facility, part of TVA's Green Invest program, aims to supply 100% clean energy to support Meta’s regional operations. Silicon Ranch will invest over $90 million in the project, which is expected to create over 350 construction jobs and be completed by the end of the year.

title: TVA & Silicon Ranch break ground on 70MW solar farm serving Meta’s Tennessee campus
summary: Ground has been broken on a new 70MW solar farm in Madison County, Tennessee, a collaboration between the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), Meta, the Jackson Energy Authority (JEA), and Silicon Ranch. This McKellar Solar Farm will supply 100 percent renewable energy to Meta's Gallatin data centers upon its expected completion by the end of 2022. Silicon Ranch will fund, own, and operate the facility, investing over $90 million in its construction.

title: Financial Firm MetaBank Rebrands as Pathward
